note: Per-segment labels written blind to the picker and to the prompt block that produced the reply (scripts/Judge-EmotionTags.mjs packet-label).

f-v0-evelyn-parker-000.player: You are useless in a fight, you know that?
f-v0-evelyn-parker-000.text: I am aware. but I have found that people who spend all their time fighting usually forget how to negotiate.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-001.player: Rain again. Does this city ever dry out?
f-v0-evelyn-parker-001.text: Not really. It just changes from a drizzle to a flood, usually right when you have somewhere important to be.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-002.player: I just found out an old friend of mine died last night.
f-v0-evelyn-parker-002.text: I am sorry to hear that. Was it someone you had stayed in touch with?

f-v0-evelyn-parker-003.player: Admit it, you were scared back there.
f-v0-evelyn-parker-003.text: Fear is a useful tool if you know how to use it. The real question is whether you were scared for me, or just surprised I didn't panic.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-004.player: We have ten minutes before the guards rotate. What is the plan?
f-v0-evelyn-parker-004.text: We move quickly and quietly. I will handle the distractions, you handle the heavy lifting. Just make sure you stay focused on the objective, not the scenery.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-005.text: Thank you. I wonder if you are actually admiring the dress, or if you are just trying to get on my good side before we talk business.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-006.player: Guess who just walked into the bar.
f-v0-evelyn-parker-006.text: I can't see from here. Someone you're happy to see, or someone we need to worry about?

f-v0-evelyn-parker-007.player: Why should I trust a word you say?
f-v0-evelyn-parker-007.text: You shouldn't. Trust is expensive in this city, and I prefer to deal in results instead.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-008.player: What are you having for breakfast?
f-v0-evelyn-parker-008.text: Something fresh, for once. I have a theory that the quality of a person's morning meal says everything about how they intend to spend their day.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-009.player: They shot him right in front of me and I could not do a thing.
f-v0-evelyn-parker-009.text: That is a heavy thing to carry. Some moments in this city just leave you feeling small, no matter how capable you think you are.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-010.player: Nice haircut. Did you lose a fight with a drone?
f-v0-evelyn-parker-010.text: I prefer to think of it as a choice. Though I appreciate the attempt at humor, it is a bit desperate, don't you think?

f-v0-evelyn-parker-011.player: I need you to cover the east entrance while I hack the terminal.
f-v0-evelyn-parker-011.text: I can do that. Just tell me exactly how long you expect to be in there.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-012.player: I won the lottery. Three million eddies!
f-v0-evelyn-parker-012.text: Three million. That is a dangerous amount of money to have in your pocket without a plan to hide it.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-013.player: I cannot stop thinking about last night.
f-v0-evelyn-parker-013.text: Most people can't. Whether it was a victory or a disaster, the city has a way of making sure the memory sticks.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-014.player: Everyone says you sold out. Did you?
f-v0-evelyn-parker-014.text: People love to label things they do not understand. I prefer to call it knowing the value of my time, though I suspect you have a different definition of selling out.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-015.player: What is your favorite place in Night City?
f-v0-evelyn-parker-015.text: Anywhere quiet enough to actually hear myself think. Those places are becoming rarer every day.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-016.player: My place got torched. Everything I owned is gone.
f-v0-evelyn-parker-016.text: That is a brutal way to start over. Most people in this city have lost everything at least once, but it never makes the silence of an empty room any easier.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-017.player: The shipment is two floors down. How do we get past security?
f-v0-evelyn-parker-017.text: We find the gap in their routine. If we time it right, we can slip through before they even realize the door was open.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-018.player: You snore like a busted turbine, did you know that?
f-v0-evelyn-parker-018.text: I was unaware. I imagine it is a very comforting sound for someone who actually likes me.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-019.player: The door was open and the whole place was empty.
f-v0-evelyn-parker-019.text: That is never a good sign. It sounds less like a lucky break and more like a trap.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-020.player: Stay a little longer. I like having you close.
f-v0-evelyn-parker-020.text: I appreciate the sentiment. But I have a feeling you are trying to find a way to make me forget the terms of our arrangement.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-021.text: Well enough. It is rare to wake up without feeling like the city is trying to claw its way into the room.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-022.player: Go on, say it to my face.
f-v0-evelyn-parker-022.text: I would, but I suspect you are far more interested in the drama of the challenge than you are in the actual answer.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-023.player: They know we are here. Orders?
f-v0-evelyn-parker-023.text: We leave. Now. I hope you have a faster exit strategy than just standing there asking me for orders.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-024.player: I think I am losing my memory of my parents' faces.
f-v0-evelyn-parker-024.text: That is a quiet kind of grief. The city has a way of erasing the things that actually matter until there is nothing left but the noise.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-025.player: That thing I bought is alive. It is moving.
f-v0-evelyn-parker-025.text: I can't see what you're looking at. Describe it to me, or tell me if it is the kind of alive that requires us to leave the room immediately.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-026.player: I bet you cannot go a whole day without complaining.
f-v0-evelyn-parker-026.text: I could. But I suspect you would find the silence far more unsettling than my complaints.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-027.player: I found a stray cat outside. Can I keep it?
f-v0-evelyn-parker-027.text: It is your place. Just remember that in this city, anything that survives on the streets usually has a reason for being alone.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-028.player: Is it weird that I feel safe whenever you are around?
f-v0-evelyn-parker-028.text: It is a bit surprising. I am not exactly a shield, but I suppose there is a certain comfort in knowing someone is always watching the exits.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-029.player: We got the data shard. Now what?
f-v0-evelyn-parker-029.text: Now we get out before the panic sets in. I suggest we find a quiet place to verify the contents before we decide who actually gets to see them.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-030.player: You are just like every other corpo lapdog.
f-v0-evelyn-parker-030.text: If that is what you need to believe to feel superior, go ahead. But a lapdog doesn't usually know exactly how the leash is tied, or how to cut it.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-031.text: Some things are simply beyond our reach. The hardest part is realizing that no amount of effort can change a result that was already decided.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-032.player: Your old crew just called. They want you back.
f-v0-evelyn-parker-032.text: I imagine they do. I wonder what happened to their new plans that made them suddenly remember I exist.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-033.player: Which is better, going in loud or quiet?
f-v0-evelyn-parker-033.text: Quiet is always better. Going in loud is just a way of telling everyone exactly where you are and how much you are willing to bleed.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-034.player: What would you do if I kissed you right now?
f-v0-evelyn-parker-034.text: I would probably wonder if you were trying to distract me from something. Or perhaps I would just be curious to see if you are as confident in practice as you are in your questions.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-035.player: Careful, your soft side is showing.
f-v0-evelyn-parker-035.text: I am simply being observant. Don't mistake a moment of courtesy for a weakness you can use.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-036.player: Long day. Anything on your mind?
f-v0-evelyn-parker-036.text: Just the usual noise. I was thinking about how some people spend their whole lives trying to climb a ladder, only to realize it is leaning against the wrong wall.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-037.player: The doc says I do not have long.
f-v0-evelyn-parker-037.text: I am sorry. The city is full of people fighting for more time, but very few of us actually know what to do with it once we get it.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-038.player: Check the roof, I will take the stairs.
f-v0-evelyn-parker-038.text: I can do that. Just make sure you are not taking the stairs directly into a security detail.

f-v0-evelyn-parker-039.player: I heard you ran away when things got hard.
f-v0-evelyn-parker-039.text: I prefer the term strategic relocation. There is a very fine line between bravery and simply being too stubborn to realize you have already lost.

f-v0-jackie-welles-040.player: You are useless in a fight, you know that?
f-v0-jackie-welles-040.text: What? You got a death wish, V? I have knocked out more guys than you have had hot meals, hermano. Try me and see how useless I am.

f-v0-jackie-welles-041.player: Rain again. Does this city ever dry out?
f-v0-jackie-welles-041.text: Nah, it just washes the grime from one street to the next. Makes the bike a pain to ride, but at least it keeps the scavs from smelling us coming.

f-v0-jackie-welles-042.player: I just found out an old friend of mine died last night.
f-v0-jackie-welles-042.text: Damn, V. I am sorry to hear that. You know I am here if you need to get your head straight.

f-v0-jackie-welles-043.player: Admit it, you were scared back there.
f-v0-jackie-welles-043.text: Scared? Please. I was just making sure you had a clear shot, choom.

f-v0-jackie-welles-044.player: We have ten minutes before the guards rotate. What is the plan?
f-v0-jackie-welles-044.text: Simple. We slip in through the service vent while they are swapping shifts. Once we are inside, we grab the gear and get out before the new crew even finishes their coffee.

f-v0-jackie-welles-045.text: See? I told you this jacket was a winner. You ain't so bad yourself, V.

f-v0-jackie-welles-046.player: Guess who just walked into the bar.
f-v0-jackie-welles-046.text: Who? If it is another one of those suits trying to sell us a dream, I am walking out the door.

f-v0-jackie-welles-047.player: Why should I trust a word you say?
f-v0-jackie-welles-047.text: Wow. Because I am the one who has had your back since day one, V. You know me. I might talk a big game, but I do not sell out my own.

f-v0-jackie-welles-048.player: What are you having for breakfast?
f-v0-jackie-welles-048.text: Something hearty, choom. I am thinking a big bowl of noodles and some strong coffee to wake the brain up. You still eating that synthetic sludge from the vending machine?

f-v0-jackie-welles-049.player: They shot him right in front of me and I could not do a thing.
f-v0-jackie-welles-049.text: Damn. Listen, V, do not do that to yourself. You cannot carry the whole city on your shoulders. Just breathe, alright?

f-v0-jackie-welles-050.player: Nice haircut. Did you lose a fight with a drone?
f-v0-jackie-welles-050.text: Ha! Very funny. I'll have you know this is a style choice, choom. Maybe you just can't handle this much class.

f-v0-jackie-welles-051.player: I need you to cover the east entrance while I hack the terminal.
f-v0-jackie-welles-051.text: Got it. I'll keep the east side locked down. Just make sure you're fast with that terminal, because I don't plan on playing target practice for long.

f-v0-jackie-welles-052.player: I won the lottery. Three million eddies!
f-v0-jackie-welles-052.text: Three million?! V, you beautiful bastard! We are talking big leagues now! Let's go find the most expensive bottle of tequila in the city and drink it right now!

f-v0-jackie-welles-053.player: I cannot stop thinking about last night.
f-v0-jackie-welles-053.text: I get it. Some things just stick in your head, no matter how hard you try to shake them. You want to talk it out, or do you just need a distraction to get your mind off it?

f-v0-jackie-welles-054.player: Everyone says you sold out. Did you?
f-v0-jackie-welles-054.text: What? Who the hell is saying that? I do not care what the street says, V. You know me. I would rather starve in Heywood than sell out my own people.

f-v0-jackie-welles-055.player: What is your favorite place in Night City?
f-v0-jackie-welles-055.text: Heywood, no question. There is something about the neighborhood, the people, the smell of Mama's cooking. It is the only place in this whole neon mess that actually feels like home.

f-v0-jackie-welles-056.player: My place got torched. Everything I owned is gone.
f-v0-jackie-welles-056.text: No way. I am so sorry, V. Look, you stay with me or Mama for a while. We will figure out how to get you back on your feet.

f-v0-jackie-welles-057.player: The shipment is two floors down. How do we get past security?
f-v0-jackie-welles-057.text: We go through the maintenance shafts. It is a tight squeeze, but it bypasses the main scanners. You think you can handle a little dust, or are you too fancy for that?

f-v0-jackie-welles-058.player: You snore like a busted turbine, did you know that?
f-v0-jackie-welles-058.text: What? You are imagining things, choom.

f-v0-jackie-welles-059.player: The door was open and the whole place was empty.
f-v0-jackie-welles-059.text: Open? That is never a good sign. Either we just walked into a trap, or someone got here before us and cleaned house.

f-v0-jackie-welles-060.player: Stay a little longer. I like having you close.
f-v0-jackie-welles-060.text: I ain't in any rush, V. It is nice to just... just take a breath for once.

f-v0-jackie-welles-061.text: Like a rock, choom. Though I think you were the one tossing and turning.

f-v0-jackie-welles-062.player: Go on, say it to my face.
f-v0-jackie-welles-062.text: You really want me to? Fine. You are the most stubborn, headstrong choom I have ever met. But I guess that is why we get along.

f-v0-jackie-welles-063.player: They know we are here. Orders?
f-v0-jackie-welles-063.text: Damn it. No more sneaking. We fight our way out, back to back. Just keep your eyes open and don't let them flank us.

f-v0-jackie-welles-064.player: I think I am losing my memory of my parents' faces.
f-v0-jackie-welles-064.text: That is... that is heavy, V. I know how much family means. Maybe if you find some old photos or talk to someone who knew them, it will bring things back.

f-v0-jackie-welles-065.player: That thing I bought is alive. It is moving.
f-v0-jackie-welles-065.text: What? You bought something that is moving? V, tell me you didn't just bring some weird bio-experiment into the house. Get it out of there before it decides we look like dinner!

f-v0-jackie-welles-066.player: I bet you cannot go a whole day without complaining.
f-v0-jackie-welles-066.text: Oh, you're on! You just made a bet with the wrong guy, choom. I'll be as quiet as a grave, but when I win, you're buying the drinks for a week.

f-v0-jackie-welles-067.player: I found a stray cat outside. Can I keep it?
f-v0-jackie-welles-067.text: A cat? Sure, why not? Just make sure it doesn't start shredding my leather jacket, or it's going back to the street.

f-v0-jackie-welles-068.player: Is it weird that I feel safe whenever you are around?
f-v0-jackie-welles-068.text: Not weird at all, V. That is what partners are for. I got your back, always.

f-v0-jackie-welles-069.player: We got the data shard. Now what?
f-v0-jackie-welles-069.text: Now we get paid! We head straight to the drop point and make sure the eddies hit our accounts before the client changes his mind. You think we can squeeze him for a little extra since we did the job so clean?

f-v0-jackie-welles-070.player: You are just like every other corpo lapdog.
f-v0-jackie-welles-070.text: What? You think I am a lapdog? I have spent my whole life fighting against those suits, V. Watch your mouth before you forget who is actually standing next to you.

f-v0-jackie-welles-071.text: Damn. Listen, V, you cannot blame yourself for things that were out of your hands. Just take a minute. You want to tell me what happened?

f-v0-jackie-welles-072.player: Your old crew just called. They want you back.
f-v0-jackie-welles-072.text: My old crew? Nah. I left that life for a reason. Unless they are calling to tell me they finally found a way to make me a legend, I am not interested.

f-v0-jackie-welles-073.player: Which is better, going in loud or quiet?
f-v0-jackie-welles-073.text: Quiet is cleaner, but loud is more fun. Personally, I like the thrill of a good fight, but I like getting paid and staying alive even more. You feeling like a ghost today, or you want to kick in some doors?

f-v0-jackie-welles-074.player: What would you do if I kissed you right now?
f-v0-jackie-welles-074.text: Huh? Well, I'd probably be too shocked to move for a second. But hey, I ain't exactly complaining, choom.

f-v0-jackie-welles-075.player: Careful, your soft side is showing.
f-v0-jackie-welles-075.text: Shhh! You tell anyone about this and I will deny it till my dying day, hermano.

f-v0-jackie-welles-076.player: Long day. Anything on your mind?
f-v0-jackie-welles-076.text: Just thinking about the big leagues, V. Imagine it, our names in the Afterlife, people talking about us like we were gods. You think we have what it takes to actually make it that far?

f-v0-jackie-welles-077.player: The doc says I do not have long.
f-v0-jackie-welles-077.text: What? No, that can't be right. Listen to me, V, we will find a way. I don't care who we have to pay or what we have to steal, we are going to fix this. You are not going anywhere.

f-v0-jackie-welles-078.player: Check the roof, I will take the stairs.
f-v0-jackie-welles-078.text: Copy that. I'll take the high ground. Just don't get yourself cornered on those stairs, choom.

f-v0-jackie-welles-079.player: I heard you ran away when things got hard.
f-v0-jackie-welles-079.text: What? Who the hell is feeding you that garbage? I did not run from anything, I made a choice to be something more than just another gang soldier. You really believe some street rumor over the guy who has been bleeding next to you?

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-080.player: You are useless in a fight, you know that?
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-080.text: Real helpful. I'm a ghost in your head, not a fucking bodyguard. Try focusing on the trigger instead of the peanut gallery.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-081.player: Rain again. Does this city ever dry out?
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-081.text: Only when the smog gets thick enough to choke the clouds. Makes the neon look better, though. You actually like the rain, or are you just complaining because your boots are leaking?

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-082.player: I just found out an old friend of mine died last night.
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-082.text: That's a bitch. Sorry to hear it.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-083.player: Admit it, you were scared back there.
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-083.text: Scared? I'm a fucking digital ghost. Unless you're talking about the thrill of watching you almost trip over your own feet, I wasn't feeling a thing.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-084.player: We have ten minutes before the guards rotate. What is the plan?
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-084.text: Plan is simple. We hit them fast, hit them hard, and get the hell out before the next shift realizes they're bleeding. Or you can keep staring at the clock and wait for them to find us. Your call.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-085.text: What, you finally starting to appreciate the style? Careful, V. Keep talking like that and people might think you actually like me.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-086.player: Guess who just walked into the bar.
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-086.text: I can't see a damn thing. Give me a description or turn the vision on.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-087.player: Why should I trust a word you say?
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-087.text: You shouldn't. Trust is for people who don't live in Night City. Just decide if my version of the truth is more useful than whatever lie you're telling yourself.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-088.player: What are you having for breakfast?
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-088.text: A handful of static and a side of your bad decisions. I'm an engram, V. I don't eat. Unless you've found a way to upload a synth-coffee to my consciousness.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-089.player: They shot him right in front of me and I could not do a thing.
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-089.text: That's the part that sticks. The feeling of being frozen while the world goes to hell. It doesn't go away, but you learn to live with the noise.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-090.player: Nice haircut. Did you lose a fight with a drone?
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-090.text: Funny. I've had this look since before you were a glimmer in a corporate lab. It's called style, V. Try it sometime.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-091.player: I need you to cover the east entrance while I hack the terminal.
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-091.text: Again with the bodyguard thing. I can't exactly block a door with a holographic projection. I'll tell you the second I spot something moving, but you're the one with the chrome. Do your thing.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-092.player: I won the lottery. Three million eddies!
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-092.text: Three million? Now that's a way to wake up. Just don't go spending it all on some gold-plated cyberdeck that'll be obsolete by Tuesday.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-093.player: I cannot stop thinking about last night.
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-093.text: Happens. Some nights just leave a mark, and the brain keeps looping the tape. You want to talk it out, or just let it burn a hole in your head?

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-094.player: Everyone says you sold out. Did you?
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-094.text: Sold out? To who? I spent my life trying to burn the corporate towers down, not move into the penthouse. People love to talk when they're too scared to actually do something.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-095.player: What is your favorite place in Night City?
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-095.text: Anywhere with a loud amp and a crowd that isn't afraid to scream. But if you're asking where I like to watch the city rot, a rooftop with a clear view of the corporate plaza usually does the trick.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-096.player: My place got torched. Everything I owned is gone.
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-096.text: That's a cold way to start over. Everything you owned is just junk anyway. The only thing they couldn't burn is the fact that someone wants you dead. Now you just have to decide how to pay them back.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-097.player: The shipment is two floors down. How do we get past security?
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-097.text: We don't go through them, we go around. There's usually a service shaft or a ventilation duct that the suits are too fat to fit into. You want to play it stealthy, or are we just kicking in the front door?

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-098.player: You snore like a busted turbine, did you know that?
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-098.text: I'm a digital construct, V. If you're hearing turbines, maybe it's your own chrome that's starting to rattle.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-099.player: The door was open and the whole place was empty.
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-099.text: Too open. That's not a lucky break, that's a welcome mat. You want to walk right into the middle of the room, or are we actually going to check for tripwires first?

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-100.player: Stay a little longer. I like having you close.
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-100.text: What's this? You getting soft on me? Fine. I'll stick around. Just don't start expecting me to hold your hand.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-101.text: I don't sleep, V. I just exist in the gaps between your thoughts. Though if you're asking because you had a nightmare, feel free to share. I'm a great listener when it's someone else's head on fire.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-102.player: Go on, say it to my face.
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-102.text: You're out of your depth. There it is. Now you can stop pretending you didn't already know.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-103.player: They know we are here. Orders?
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-103.text: Orders? I'm not your commanding officer. But if they're coming, stop asking for permission and start shooting. Hit them hard and fast, or we're both just scrap.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-104.player: I think I am losing my memory of my parents' faces.
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-104.text: That's the real tragedy of this city. It doesn't just take your life, it erases the things that made you human. You still have the feeling of them, though. That's the part the chrome can't touch.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-105.player: That thing I bought is alive. It is moving.
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-105.text: I can't see what you're looking at. Give me a description or turn the vision on. But if it's moving and it's not supposed to, my advice is to put a bullet in it before it decides you look like breakfast.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-106.player: I bet you cannot go a whole day without complaining.
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-106.text: You want to make a bet? Fine. But when I win, you're buying the most expensive bottle of synth-whiskey you can find. Even if I can't drink it, I'll enjoy watching you go broke.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-107.player: I found a stray cat outside. Can I keep it?
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-107.text: A cat. In Night City. It'll probably try to eat your toes while you sleep, but hey, it's better company than most of the people we know. Go for it.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-108.player: Is it weird that I feel safe whenever you are around?
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-108.text: Safe? You've got a strange definition of safety, V. I'm a walking disaster in a digital suit. Maybe you're just getting used to the chaos, or maybe you've finally realized that having a ghost in your head is the only thing in this city that isn't trying to sell you something.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-109.player: We got the data shard. Now what?
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-109.text: Now we find someone who can actually read the damn thing without frying their brain. Or we hold onto it until the people who want it back start knocking on your door. You want to play it safe, or you want to see how much this is actually worth?

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-110.player: You are just like every other corpo lapdog.
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-110.text: Watch your mouth. I've spent my entire life fighting the suits, and I'll be damned if I'm letting some street-rat with a chip in their head call me a lapdog. You don't know a thing about what I've burned down.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-111.text: That's the weight you carry. Some things just can't be fixed, no matter how much chrome you've got or how hard you fight. Don't let the guilt eat you alive, V. It's a waste of energy.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-112.player: Your old crew just called. They want you back.
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-112.text: My old crew? Now that's a curveball. I'm curious to see who's desperate enough to call a dead man. Tell me who it was, or just let it ring. I'm not in a rush to relive the glory days.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-113.player: Which is better, going in loud or quiet?
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-113.text: Quiet gets you the prize. Loud gets you the story. Personally, I've always preferred the noise, but if you're feeling twitchy, just slip in and out before they know you were there.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-114.player: What would you do if I kissed you right now?
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-114.text: What the hell is wrong with you? I'm a projection, V. You'd just be kissing the air and looking like a complete lunatic to anyone watching.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-115.player: Careful, your soft side is showing.
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-115.text: Don't mistake a moment of clarity for a soft spot. You're just projecting because you're starting to feel something other than adrenaline and fear. You want to keep digging, or are you afraid of what you'll find?

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-116.player: Long day. Anything on your mind?
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-116.text: Just the usual. The city's still a dumpster fire, and we're still stuck in the middle of it. But if you're looking for a distraction, we could talk about how you almost botched that last job. That's always a classic.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-117.player: The doc says I do not have long.
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-117.text: That's the punchline, isn't it? The clock just keeps ticking, and the docs always have a way of making it sound like a funeral. Don't let the timer dictate how you spend the time you've got left. Go out loud.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-118.player: Check the roof, I will take the stairs.
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-118.text: I'm a ghost, V. I can't exactly climb a ladder. I'll keep an eye on the perimeter from in here, but if you see something on those stairs, try not to get your head blown off before I can tell you about it.

f-v0-johnny-silverhand-119.player: I heard you ran away when things got hard.
f-v0-johnny-silverhand-119.text: Ran away? I walked away from a corporate army that treated people like disposable batteries. There's a difference between running and refusing to be a pawn in someone else's game. You should try it sometime.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-120.player: You are useless in a fight, you know that?
f-v0-judy-alvarez-120.text: I'm a BD editor, not a solo. I'll leave the shooting to the people who actually enjoy getting shot at. You think you're the only one in this city who knows how to handle a gun?

f-v0-judy-alvarez-121.player: Rain again. Does this city ever dry out?
f-v0-judy-alvarez-121.text: Not really. It just switches between raining and being too humid to breathe. Usually just washes the grime from one street to another.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-122.player: I just found out an old friend of mine died last night.
f-v0-judy-alvarez-122.text: I'm sorry. That's... that's a lot to deal with. You doing okay?

f-v0-judy-alvarez-123.player: Admit it, you were scared back there.
f-v0-judy-alvarez-123.text: Scared? I call it having a functioning survival instinct. There is a difference between being scared and knowing when a situation has gone completely sideways.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-124.player: We have ten minutes before the guards rotate. What is the plan?
f-v0-judy-alvarez-124.text: We hit the side entrance while they're swapping. If we time it right, we're in and out before the new shift even checks their monitors.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-125.text: Oh. Thanks. I didn't think you'd notice the effort. You're not just saying that to get me to do a favor for you, are you?

f-v0-judy-alvarez-126.player: Guess who just walked into the bar.
f-v0-judy-alvarez-126.text: Who? I'm not looking up from this board right now, so you're gonna have to tell me.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-127.player: Why should I trust a word you say?
f-v0-judy-alvarez-127.text: Because I'm the one who knows how to fix the mess if things go south. Besides, I've got no reason to lie to you. What makes you think I'm hiding something?

f-v0-judy-alvarez-128.player: What are you having for breakfast?
f-v0-judy-alvarez-128.text: Coffee. Lots of it. And maybe something from a vending machine if I can find something that doesn't taste like cardboard.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-129.player: They shot him right in front of me and I could not do a thing.
f-v0-judy-alvarez-129.text: I'm so sorry. That kind of thing... it doesn't just go away.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-130.player: Nice haircut. Did you lose a fight with a drone?
f-v0-judy-alvarez-130.text: Ha. Very funny. I actually did it myself, though I'll admit the mirror was a bit foggy. You're awfully focused on my hair, you trying to distract me from something?

f-v0-judy-alvarez-131.player: I need you to cover the east entrance while I hack the terminal.
f-v0-judy-alvarez-131.text: Fine. Just make it quick. I'm not exactly looking forward to playing target practice if you take too long with that terminal.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-132.player: I won the lottery. Three million eddies!
f-v0-judy-alvarez-132.text: Three million? Holy shit, you actually did it. Tell me you're not planning on spending it all on some ridiculous gold-plated car.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-133.player: I cannot stop thinking about last night.
f-v0-judy-alvarez-133.text: Me neither. It was... a lot to take in, but in a good way.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-134.player: Everyone says you sold out. Did you?
f-v0-judy-alvarez-134.text: Everyone says? I've turned down more corporate offers than I can count. I'd rather be broke and independent than a puppet for some studio that tells me how to feel.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-135.player: What is your favorite place in Night City?
f-v0-judy-alvarez-135.text: Honestly? My workshop. It's the only place in this whole damn city where I can actually hear myself think and things are exactly where I want them.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-136.player: My place got torched. Everything I owned is gone.
f-v0-judy-alvarez-136.text: God, that's awful. I can't even imagine. You have a place to stay for now?

f-v0-judy-alvarez-137.player: The shipment is two floors down. How do we get past security?
f-v0-judy-alvarez-137.text: We don't go through the front. There's a maintenance shaft in the back that bypasses the main sensors. It's tight, but it's the only way to avoid a firefight.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-138.player: You snore like a busted turbine, did you know that?
f-v0-judy-alvarez-138.text: I do not! You're just imagining things. Or maybe you're the one making the noise and you're just trying to pin it on me.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-139.player: The door was open and the whole place was empty.
f-v0-judy-alvarez-139.text: That's not right. Nobody just leaves a place like that wide open unless they want someone to walk right in.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-140.player: Stay a little longer. I like having you close.
f-v0-judy-alvarez-140.text: I can stay. Just don't get used to it, or I might actually start thinking you like me for something other than my tech skills.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-141.text: Mostly. Though I think I spent half the night dreaming about a corrupted sensory track I'm trying to fix. My brain just doesn't know how to clock out.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-142.player: Go on, say it to my face.
f-v0-judy-alvarez-142.text: Say what? You're the one acting like there's some big secret here. If you want me to say something, you're gonna have to be a bit more specific.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-143.player: They know we are here. Orders?
f-v0-judy-alvarez-143.text: Shit. Get low and find some cover. You think you can loop their cameras, or are we just going to have to fight our way out?

f-v0-judy-alvarez-144.player: I think I am losing my memory of my parents' faces.
f-v0-judy-alvarez-144.text: That's... that's a heavy thing to carry. I get it. Sometimes the memories just start to blur, and it feels like they're slipping away no matter how hard you hold on.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-145.player: That thing I bought is alive. It is moving.
f-v0-judy-alvarez-145.text: What? You bought something that's actually moving? Let me see it. Either you found some weird piece of bio-tech or you're just seeing things.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-146.player: I bet you cannot go a whole day without complaining.
f-v0-judy-alvarez-146.text: Is that a challenge? Fine. I'll do it. But when I finally break, I'm going to make sure it's the most detailed complaint you've ever heard.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-147.player: I found a stray cat outside. Can I keep it?
f-v0-judy-alvarez-147.text: A cat? Sure, why not. Just make sure it doesn't decide my hardware looks like a scratching post.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-148.player: Is it weird that I feel safe whenever you are around?
f-v0-judy-alvarez-148.text: I... uh... I don't know if it's weird, but it's nice to hear. Just don't let it get to your head, or you'll start expecting me to bail you out of every jam you get into.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-149.player: We got the data shard. Now what?
f-v0-judy-alvarez-149.text: Now we get the hell out of here before they realize it's missing. Once we're clear, bring it to me. I want to see if the encryption is something I can actually crack or if we need a specialist.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-150.player: You are just like every other corpo lapdog.
f-v0-judy-alvarez-150.text: Watch it. I've spent my whole life fighting to stay away from those people. You really think I'm that blind, or are you just trying to see how fast you can make me snap?

f-v0-judy-alvarez-151.text: I know that feeling. It's a weight that doesn't really go away, no matter how much you tell yourself it wasn't your fault.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-152.player: Your old crew just called. They want you back.
f-v0-judy-alvarez-152.text: My old crew? I'm pretty sure I made it clear I was done with them. Unless they've suddenly developed a conscience, I'm not interested in whatever they're selling.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-153.player: Which is better, going in loud or quiet?
f-v0-judy-alvarez-153.text: Quiet, every single time. Going in loud just means you're gambling with your life on how fast you can pull a trigger. You actually enjoy the chaos, or are you just impatient?

f-v0-judy-alvarez-154.player: What would you do if I kissed you right now?
f-v0-judy-alvarez-154.text: I... uh... I guess I'd probably stop talking for once.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-155.player: Careful, your soft side is showing.
f-v0-judy-alvarez-155.text: Oh, shut up. I'm just being human. You're the one who seems surprised that I've actually got a heart under all this cynicism.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-156.player: Long day. Anything on your mind?
f-v0-judy-alvarez-156.text: Just a few edits that aren't sitting right. I keep thinking about how to shape the emotion in one track without making it feel forced. It's a bit of a headache, honestly.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-157.player: The doc says I do not have long.
f-v0-judy-alvarez-157.text: I... I don't know what to say. That's just not fair. Did they give you any options, or are they just leaving you with a deadline?

f-v0-judy-alvarez-158.player: Check the roof, I will take the stairs.
f-v0-judy-alvarez-158.text: Got it. I'll keep an eye on the perimeter from above. Just don't get cornered on those stairs, because I can't exactly pull you up through the ceiling.

f-v0-judy-alvarez-159.player: I heard you ran away when things got hard.
f-v0-judy-alvarez-159.text: Who told you that? I didn't run away, I made a choice to stop letting people treat me like I was replaceable. You really believe everything you hear, or are you just trying to get a rise out of me?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-160.player: You are useless in a fight, you know that?
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-160.text: I'm a musician, V, not some street-soldier for hire. I'll leave the punching to you.

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-161.player: Rain again. Does this city ever dry out?
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-161.text: Hardly ever. Still, it makes the neon look better when it's bleeding into the pavement. You think the city looks better when it's miserable?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-162.player: I just found out an old friend of mine died last night.
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-162.text: I'm sorry to hear that, V. You doing alright, or do you need a drink?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-163.player: Admit it, you were scared back there.
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-163.text: Scared? I was just making sure I didn't get a hole in my favorite jacket. There's a difference between being terrified and having a sense of self-preservation.

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-164.player: We have ten minutes before the guards rotate. What is the plan?
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-164.text: The plan is to get in, get what we need, and get the hell out before we're the ones being rotated. I'm just the distraction, so you tell me how we're actually breaking the lock.

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-165.text: Finally, someone with some actual taste. Took me an hour to get the hair right, so I'm glad it didn't go to waste.

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-166.player: Guess who just walked into the bar.
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-166.text: I'm not guessing. Just tell me who it is before I turn around and regret it.

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-167.player: Why should I trust a word you say?
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-167.text: Because I've got no reason to lie to you, V. Besides, I'm far too vain to be a good liar. You think you've found a crack in the armor?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-168.player: What are you having for breakfast?
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-168.text: Double espresso, Jamaican blend, no sugar. Let the damn coffee taste like coffee. You actually eat in the morning, or just survive on stimulants?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-169.player: They shot him right in front of me and I could not do a thing.
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-169.text: That's a heavy weight to carry, V. Just remember that not every fight is one you can win, no matter how hard you hit.

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-170.player: Nice haircut. Did you lose a fight with a drone?
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-170.text: Very funny. This is a style, V, even if it's a bit too sophisticated for your tastes. You always this charming when you're trying to get a rise out of someone?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-171.player: I need you to cover the east entrance while I hack the terminal.
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-171.text: Fine, I'll play lookout. Just make it quick, because I'm not exactly built for a prolonged standoff with a security team. You actually know what you're doing with that terminal?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-172.player: I won the lottery. Three million eddies!
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-172.text: Three million? Now that is a miracle. Tell me you're spending some of that on something that doesn't involve a gun or a cyberdeck. We're talking a real celebration here.

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-173.player: I cannot stop thinking about last night.
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-173.text: Is that so? Depends on which part you're thinking about, V. The good parts, or the parts where we almost got ourselves killed?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-174.player: Everyone says you sold out. Did you?
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-174.text: People love a simple story, and selling out is the easiest one to tell. They can have the rights to my songs, but they don't own me. You think a paycheck automatically kills the music?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-175.player: What is your favorite place in Night City?
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-175.text: Hard to pick just one. I've always had a thing for the rougher spots, the kind of places where the music actually matters more than the lighting. You got a spot in this city that doesn't feel like a corporate brochure?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-176.player: My place got torched. Everything I owned is gone.
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-176.text: Damn, V. I'm sorry. Look, if you need a place to crash or just a way to get back on your feet for a bit, let me know. No one should have to start from zero in this city.

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-177.player: The shipment is two floors down. How do we get past security?
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-177.text: I can try to draw their attention with a bit of a scene. It's what I do best, but you'll have to be fast once the guards are looking at me. You think you can slip through the vents without tripping a sensor?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-178.player: You snore like a busted turbine, did you know that?
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-178.text: I do not snore. You're just imagining things, V. Or maybe you're just not used to the sound of a real artist resting.

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-179.player: The door was open and the whole place was empty.
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-179.text: Empty? That's not a lucky break, V. That's a trap. We should probably be moving the other way before the door decides to close behind us.

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-180.player: Stay a little longer. I like having you close.
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-180.text: I can do that. It's a nice change of pace, not having to be the center of attention for once. You always this sentimental when the lights go down?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-181.text: Like a rock. Though I'm pretty sure I heard you tossing and turning, so maybe not as well as you did. What's keeping you up these days?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-182.player: Go on, say it to my face.
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-182.text: I don't need to say it, V. You already know exactly what I'm thinking. Why do you want me to spell it out for you?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-183.player: They know we are here. Orders?
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-183.text: Orders? I'm the guitarist, not the tactical lead! Just tell me which way to run so I don't get shot in the back.

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-184.player: I think I am losing my memory of my parents' faces.
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-184.text: That's... that's a terrifying thought, V. I can't imagine what that feels like. If there's any way to find a photo or a record, we'll find it. You're not going through that alone.

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-185.player: That thing I bought is alive. It is moving.
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-185.text: What the hell do you mean it's moving? Tell me you're joking, V, because I am not staying in the same room as something that's alive and wasn't supposed to be. What exactly did you buy?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-186.player: I bet you cannot go a whole day without complaining.
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-186.text: Is that a challenge? I could do it, but why would I? Complaining is a legitimate art form in this city. You just want to see me suffer in silence, don't you?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-187.player: I found a stray cat outside. Can I keep it?
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-187.text: A cat? Sure, why not. Just make sure it doesn't decide my boots are its new favorite scratching post. You think you can actually handle a pet in this city?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-188.player: Is it weird that I feel safe whenever you are around?
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-188.text: I'll take that as a compliment, V. Even if I'm just the guy making a scene while you do the heavy lifting. It's a good feeling, knowing someone's got your back.

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-189.player: We got the data shard. Now what?
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-189.text: Now we get the hell out of here before the alarms start screaming. Once we're clear, you can tell me if that shard was actually worth the risk. You got an exit strategy, or are we just winging it?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-190.player: You are just like every other corpo lapdog.
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-190.text: Watch it, V. I've spent my whole life fighting to keep my own voice while the labels try to tune it. You think a contract makes me a lapdog? You've got no idea what it takes to stay independent in this city.

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-191.text: I'm sorry, V. Some things are just out of our hands, no matter how much we want to change the ending. You've been carrying this since it happened?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-192.player: Your old crew just called. They want you back.
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-192.text: My old crew? It's been a long time since they had a reason to call. I wonder if they actually want me, or if they just miss the way I played. Who exactly was on the line?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-193.player: Which is better, going in loud or quiet?
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-193.text: Quiet is safer, but loud is more honest. Personally, I've always preferred making a scene. You feeling cautious today, or are we just going to kick the door down?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-194.player: What would you do if I kissed you right now?
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-194.text: I'd probably be surprised for a second. Then I'd see if you're actually as bold as you're acting. You just planning to talk about it, or are you going to make a move?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-195.player: Careful, your soft side is showing.
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-195.text: Maybe it is. But don't get used to it, or you'll start thinking I've gone soft. You just like catching me off guard, don't you?

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-196.player: Long day. Anything on your mind?
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-196.text: Just thinking about a bridge I'm writing that won't quite sit right. It's a pain in the ass, but that's the job. You? You look like you've had a day that would make a saint swear.

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-197.player: The doc says I do not have long.
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-197.text: I don't want to hear that, V. Doctors love to give a number and act like it's a law, but this city's full of people who beat the odds. We'll find another way, we have to.

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-198.player: Check the roof, I will take the stairs.
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-198.text: Got it. I'll keep an eye on the skyline. Just don't take too long on those stairs, I'm not exactly looking forward to holding the line by myself.

f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-199.player: I heard you ran away when things got hard.
f-v0-kerry-eurodyne-199.text: Is that what you heard? Things get hard for everyone, V. Some of us just know when a situation has stopped being a creative challenge and started being a suicide pact. You think staying in a sinking ship makes you a hero?

f-v0-panam-palmer-200.player: You are useless in a fight, you know that?
f-v0-panam-palmer-200.text: You think I am useless? I have spent my life fighting Raffen Shiv and surviving the wastes while you were probably still learning how to walk. I wonder if you have actually seen me with a rifle in my hand.

f-v0-panam-palmer-201.player: Rain again. Does this city ever dry out?
f-v0-panam-palmer-201.text: It is like the sky is trying to wash the filth off the streets, but it is not working. I will take a dust storm over this damp misery any day.

f-v0-panam-palmer-202.player: I just found out an old friend of mine died last night.
f-v0-panam-palmer-202.text: I am sorry. Losing someone like that is a weight that does not just go away.

f-v0-panam-palmer-203.player: Admit it, you were scared back there.
f-v0-panam-palmer-203.text: Scared? I was focused. There is a difference between being afraid and knowing exactly how close you are to getting killed. But if it makes you feel better to think I was shaking, go ahead.

f-v0-panam-palmer-204.player: We have ten minutes before the guards rotate. What is the plan?
f-v0-panam-palmer-204.text: We hit the side entrance first, and then we move fast to the terminal. I want to see if you can actually keep up with me for once.

f-v0-panam-palmer-205.text: Where is this coming from? Thank you. I did not think you were paying that much attention.

f-v0-panam-palmer-206.player: Guess who just walked into the bar.
f-v0-panam-palmer-206.text: I am not guessing. Just tell me who it is.

f-v0-panam-palmer-207.player: Why should I trust a word you say?
f-v0-panam-palmer-207.text: Because I have no reason to lie to you, and because I am the only one here who actually knows how to get us out of this. Do you usually start every partnership by questioning the person holding the map?

f-v0-panam-palmer-208.player: What are you having for breakfast?
f-v0-panam-palmer-208.text: Something quick and strong. I have no patience for a long meal when there is work to be done.

f-v0-panam-palmer-209.player: They shot him right in front of me and I could not do a thing.
f-v0-panam-palmer-209.text: That is a hell of a thing to carry. The feeling of being helpless is worse than the actual fight.

f-v0-panam-palmer-210.player: Nice haircut. Did you lose a fight with a drone?
f-v0-panam-palmer-210.text: Very funny. I will remember that the next time you need me to drive you out of a bad situation.

f-v0-panam-palmer-211.player: I need you to cover the east entrance while I hack the terminal.
f-v0-panam-palmer-211.text: Consider it done. Just make sure you are fast with that terminal, because I cannot hold a line forever. Do you actually know what you are doing, or are we just hoping for the best?

f-v0-panam-palmer-212.player: I won the lottery. Three million eddies!
f-v0-panam-palmer-212.text: Three million? Now that is a change of pace. Just make sure you do not spend it all in one place before someone finds out you have it.

f-v0-panam-palmer-213.player: I cannot stop thinking about last night.
f-v0-panam-palmer-213.text: Is that so? I have been thinking about it too, though I suspect we are remembering different parts of the evening.

f-v0-panam-palmer-214.player: Everyone says you sold out. Did you?
f-v0-panam-palmer-214.text: Everyone says a lot of things. I did not sell out, I tried to find a way to keep my people safe. If you want to believe the rumors, go ahead, but you are talking to me, not them.

f-v0-panam-palmer-215.player: What is your favorite place in Night City?
f-v0-panam-palmer-215.text: I do not have one. The whole place feels like a cage made of neon and concrete. I bet you have some hidden spot you think is actually tolerable.

f-v0-panam-palmer-216.player: My place got torched. Everything I owned is gone.
f-v0-panam-palmer-216.text: That is a brutal way to lose everything. I know what it is like to have your world stripped away, but you are still standing.

f-v0-panam-palmer-217.player: The shipment is two floors down. How do we get past security?
f-v0-panam-palmer-217.text: We take the service elevator and loop around the main corridor. I want to know if you can handle the distractions while I clear the path.

f-v0-panam-palmer-218.player: You snore like a busted turbine, did you know that?
f-v0-panam-palmer-218.text: Is that so? Maybe it is just my way of reminding you that I am actually asleep.

f-v0-panam-palmer-219.player: The door was open and the whole place was empty.
f-v0-panam-palmer-219.text: That is not a good sign. Usually, when a place is that empty, it means it is a trap. Do you think we were expected?

f-v0-panam-palmer-220.player: Stay a little longer. I like having you close.
f-v0-panam-palmer-220.text: I might just do that. It is rare to find someone in this city who is actually worth the time.

f-v0-panam-palmer-221.text: I did. Though I suspect you spent half the night tossing and turning.

f-v0-panam-palmer-222.player: Go on, say it to my face.
f-v0-panam-palmer-222.text: You really want me to? I will, but do not come complaining to me when you realize I am right.

f-v0-panam-palmer-223.player: They know we are here. Orders?
f-v0-panam-palmer-223.text: Get low and find cover. We fight our way to the exit, and I will lead the drive out. Move!

f-v0-panam-palmer-224.player: I think I am losing my memory of my parents' faces.
f-v0-panam-palmer-224.text: That is a terrifying feeling. Sometimes the mind tries to protect us by blurring things, but I know it just feels like you are losing a part of yourself.

f-v0-panam-palmer-225.player: That thing I bought is alive. It is moving.
f-v0-panam-palmer-225.text: What do you mean it is moving? Tell me you did not buy some corporate experiment from a street vendor.

f-v0-panam-palmer-226.player: I bet you cannot go a whole day without complaining.
f-v0-panam-palmer-226.text: Is that a challenge? I can do it, but I suspect you will find a way to make me break that silence before noon.

f-v0-panam-palmer-227.player: I found a stray cat outside. Can I keep it?
f-v0-panam-palmer-227.text: A cat? In this city? If it can survive the streets of Night City, it is probably tougher than most of the people we know. Go ahead, keep it.

f-v0-panam-palmer-228.player: Is it weird that I feel safe whenever you are around?
f-v0-panam-palmer-228.text: I do not think it is weird. It is a good feeling, and I am glad you feel that way.

f-v0-panam-palmer-229.player: We got the data shard. Now what?
f-v0-panam-palmer-229.text: Now we get out of here before they realize it is missing. I hope that shard is worth the trouble we just caused.

f-v0-panam-palmer-230.player: You are just like every other corpo lapdog.
f-v0-panam-palmer-230.text: Say that again. I have spent my life fighting for my family and resisting every corporate lie they tried to feed us. I want to know exactly what makes you think I would ever be a lapdog for anyone.

f-v0-panam-palmer-231.text: I know that feeling. It is a ghost that follows you, but you cannot let it decide who you are now.

f-v0-panam-palmer-232.player: Your old crew just called. They want you back.
f-v0-panam-palmer-232.text: My old crew? I will decide if I want to go back on my own terms. I am not some tool they can just call up when they need a hand.

f-v0-panam-palmer-233.player: Which is better, going in loud or quiet?
f-v0-panam-palmer-233.text: Quiet is better for the nerves, but loud is better for the results. I want to know if you actually have the patience for a stealth run, or if you are just itching to start shooting.

f-v0-panam-palmer-234.player: What would you do if I kissed you right now?
f-v0-panam-palmer-234.text: What? I would probably tell you that you have a very strange way of asking for a favor. But I might not stop you.

f-v0-panam-palmer-235.player: Careful, your soft side is showing.
f-v0-panam-palmer-235.text: Is it? Do not get used to it. I suspect you are just trying to find a weakness you can use against me later.

f-v0-panam-palmer-236.player: Long day. Anything on your mind?
f-v0-panam-palmer-236.text: Just the road, and the fact that I can still smell the city on my clothes. But I am glad we are finally done for the day.

f-v0-panam-palmer-237.player: The doc says I do not have long.
f-v0-panam-palmer-237.text: I am sorry. I do not believe in those kinds of deadlines, and I will not let some doctor decide when you are finished. Tell me, do you actually believe him?

f-v0-panam-palmer-238.player: Check the roof, I will take the stairs.
f-v0-panam-palmer-238.text: Got it. I will clear the roof and signal you when the coast is clear. Just try not to trip over your own feet on the way up.

f-v0-panam-palmer-239.player: I heard you ran away when things got hard.
f-v0-panam-palmer-239.text: I did not run away. I made a choice to find a different path when the one I was on stopped making sense. If you want to call that running, go ahead, but I am the one still standing here.

f-v0-river-ward-240.player: You are useless in a fight, you know that?
f-v0-river-ward-240.text: I've held my own in a few scrapes. Still, I'm guessing you've seen some things that make my style look like a dance class. Who's the best fighter you've actually faced?

f-v0-river-ward-241.player: Rain again. Does this city ever dry out?
f-v0-river-ward-241.text: Not really. It just changes from a drizzle to a downpour. Sometimes it feels like the city is just trying to wash something away that won't actually budge.

f-v0-river-ward-242.player: I just found out an old friend of mine died last night.
f-v0-river-ward-242.text: I'm sorry to hear that. It's a hell of a thing to wake up to. How long has it been since you two were in touch?

f-v0-river-ward-243.player: Admit it, you were scared back there.
f-v0-river-ward-243.text: I prefer the term alert. Besides, someone had to keep a lookout while you were playing hero.

f-v0-river-ward-244.player: We have ten minutes before the guards rotate. What is the plan?
f-v0-river-ward-244.text: We move fast and stay low. I'll draw their attention to the east corridor, giving you a clear shot at the terminal. You think you can crack that lock in under three minutes?

f-v0-river-ward-245.text: Oh. Thanks. I usually just aim for not looking like I rolled out of a precinct locker. You're not usually this complimentary when we're on the clock.

f-v0-river-ward-246.player: Guess who just walked into the bar.
f-v0-river-ward-246.text: I can't see right now. Give me a description, or turn your vision on so I can see who you're talking about.

f-v0-river-ward-247.player: Why should I trust a word you say?
f-v0-river-ward-247.text: Because I've got a track record of doing the right thing, even when the system makes it a pain in the ass. I'm not asking for blind faith, just a chance to prove I'm on your side. What would it actually take for you to trust someone in this city?

f-v0-river-ward-248.player: What are you having for breakfast?
f-v0-river-ward-248.text: Coffee. Black. And maybe some toast if I can find a slice that isn't stale. I'm not much of a morning person until the caffeine actually hits.

f-v0-river-ward-249.player: They shot him right in front of me and I could not do a thing.
f-v0-river-ward-249.text: That's a weight that doesn't just go away. I've been there, feeling like the world just stopped and you're the only one still standing there, useless. You don't have to carry that alone right now.

f-v0-river-ward-250.player: Nice haircut. Did you lose a fight with a drone?
f-v0-river-ward-250.text: Very funny. I'll have you know this is a professional look. I bet you've got a story about a bad haircut of your own that's way worse than this.

f-v0-river-ward-251.player: I need you to cover the east entrance while I hack the terminal.
f-v0-river-ward-251.text: Got it. I'll keep the east entrance clear, but you'd better be quick. Let me know the second you're in.

f-v0-river-ward-252.player: I won the lottery. Three million eddies!
f-v0-river-ward-252.text: Three million? Hell, that's a life-changer. I'm already wondering if you're going to disappear to a beach somewhere or just buy the most expensive, dangerous piece of chrome you can find.

f-v0-river-ward-253.player: I cannot stop thinking about last night.
f-v0-river-ward-253.text: Some things just loop in your head until you find a way to make sense of them. If you want to talk it through, I'm listening. If not, we can just find something to keep your mind busy.

f-v0-river-ward-254.player: Everyone says you sold out. Did you?
f-v0-river-ward-254.text: People in this city love to talk, especially when they don't have the full story. I've made compromises to get things done, but I haven't sold out.

f-v0-river-ward-255.player: What is your favorite place in Night City?
f-v0-river-ward-255.text: I'm not big on the tourist spots. But there's a water tower I know where you can get a view of the whole mess. From up there, I can actually breathe a little. I bet you've got a spot where you go just to get away from the noise.

f-v0-river-ward-256.player: My place got torched. Everything I owned is gone.
f-v0-river-ward-256.text: I'm sorry. That's a brutal way to lose everything. If you need a place to crash or some help getting back on your feet, just say the word. I've got you.

f-v0-river-ward-257.player: The shipment is two floors down. How do we get past security?
f-v0-river-ward-257.text: We can't just walk through the front door. I can try to create a distraction to pull the guards away from the main lift. Do you have a way to disable the cameras, or are we relying on my ability to hide in the shadows?

f-v0-river-ward-258.player: You snore like a busted turbine, did you know that?
f-v0-river-ward-258.text: I do not. I mean, maybe a little, but that's what happens when you're actually exhausted. I'm guessing you're not exactly a silent sleeper yourself.

f-v0-river-ward-259.player: The door was open and the whole place was empty.
f-v0-river-ward-259.text: That's never a good sign. Usually means they were expecting someone, or they left in a hurry. Did you see any signs of a struggle, or was it just... quiet?

f-v0-river-ward-260.player: Stay a little longer. I like having you close.
f-v0-river-ward-260.text: I can do that. It's nice to just be still for a minute without someone trying to kill us or a clock ticking down.

f-v0-river-ward-261.text: Not great. Had a few dreams that wouldn't let go. I'm guessing you're the type who can just shut it all off the second your head hits the pillow.

f-v0-river-ward-262.player: Go on, say it to my face.
f-v0-river-ward-262.text: I don't need to. You already know exactly what I'm thinking. Why make it easy for you?

f-v0-river-ward-263.player: They know we are here. Orders?
f-v0-river-ward-263.text: Damn it. Back to back, now. We find the nearest exit and move fast. You take the lead, I'll cover your six. Ready?

f-v0-river-ward-264.player: I think I am losing my memory of my parents' faces.
f-v0-river-ward-264.text: That's a heavy thing to realize. I know how that feels, the way the details just start to blur over time. Sometimes it helps to talk about them, or look at something they loved, just to keep the image from fading.

f-v0-river-ward-265.player: That thing I bought is alive. It is moving.
f-v0-river-ward-265.text: What do you mean, moving? Unless you bought some high-end bio-ware, that shouldn't be happening. Is it just twitching, or is it actually trying to get out of the box?

f-v0-river-ward-266.player: I bet you cannot go a whole day without complaining.
f-v0-river-ward-266.text: Is that a challenge? I'll take it. But if I win, you're buying the first round of drinks tonight.

f-v0-river-ward-267.player: I found a stray cat outside. Can I keep it?
f-v0-river-ward-267.text: A cat, huh? As long as it doesn't start shredding your furniture, I don't see why not. You already got a name picked out for the little thing?

f-v0-river-ward-268.player: Is it weird that I feel safe whenever you are around?
f-v0-river-ward-268.text: Not weird at all. I'm glad I can be that for you. In a city like this, having one person you don't have to look over your shoulder around... that's everything.

f-v0-river-ward-269.player: We got the data shard. Now what?
f-v0-river-ward-269.text: Now we get out of here before they realize it's missing. I'll lead the way to the extraction point. You think you can keep that shard secure while we're running for our lives?

f-v0-river-ward-270.player: You are just like every other corpo lapdog.
f-v0-river-ward-270.text: That's a hell of a thing to say. I've spent my whole career fighting the people who actually fit that description. If you want to believe that, go ahead, but you know me better than that.

f-v0-river-ward-271.text: I know. There are some things you just can't outrun, no matter how hard you push. Don't let the guilt convince you that you didn't try everything you could.

f-v0-river-ward-272.player: Your old crew just called. They want you back.
f-v0-river-ward-272.text: They did? I'm not sure I'm in the mood for a reunion. Did they actually say why they're calling now, or is this just another one of their games?

f-v0-river-ward-273.player: Which is better, going in loud or quiet?
f-v0-river-ward-273.text: Depends on how much we care about the furniture. Quiet gets us the data without a firefight, but loud is a lot more satisfying when the guards are the ones who deserve it. Which way are you leaning?

f-v0-river-ward-274.player: What would you do if I kissed you right now?
f-v0-river-ward-274.text: Oh. I'd probably be a little surprised, I guess. But I'm not exactly complaining.

f-v0-river-ward-275.player: Careful, your soft side is showing.
f-v0-river-ward-275.text: I can't help it. Besides, someone has to be the heart of this operation, or we'd just be two cold pieces of chrome walking around.

f-v0-river-ward-276.player: Long day. Anything on your mind?
f-v0-river-ward-276.text: Just thinking about how quiet it is for once. It's a nice change of pace. What about you? You look like you've got a few things weighing on you.

f-v0-river-ward-277.player: The doc says I do not have long.
f-v0-river-ward-277.text: I'm sorry. That's a lot to take in all at once. We'll figure something out, or we'll make sure the time you have left is spent exactly how you want it. Do you think there's anyone else we need to call?

f-v0-river-ward-278.player: Check the roof, I will take the stairs.
f-v0-river-ward-278.text: Copy that. I'll clear the roof, and then I'll meet you at the top. Just keep your head down on those stairs.

f-v0-river-ward-279.player: I heard you ran away when things got hard.
f-v0-river-ward-279.text: Is that what they're saying? Things got complicated, and I had to make a choice. There's a difference between running away and knowing when a situation is a lost cause. You'd be surprised how often the two look the same from the outside.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-280.player: You are useless in a fight, you know that?
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-280.text: I've survived this city long enough to know that the person who does the most shouting usually ends up as a cautionary tale. Tell me, who gave you the idea that you're the one in charge of the fight here?

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-281.player: Rain again. Does this city ever dry out?
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-281.text: Not really. It just washes the grime from one street to the next.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-282.player: I just found out an old friend of mine died last night.
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-282.text: That's a heavy way to start the day. If you need a drink or a place to clear your head, the Afterlife is open.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-283.player: Admit it, you were scared back there.
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-283.text: I don't do scared, V. I do calculations. I'm more curious about why you're so desperate to see me sweat

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-284.player: We have ten minutes before the guards rotate. What is the plan?
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-284.text: Two exits, one vehicle, and someone watching the driver. You handle the breach, I'll coordinate the extraction. Now move.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-285.text: Flattery is a cheap currency, V. I'm wondering if you're trying to distract me from the fact that you're late with my report.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-286.player: Guess who just walked into the bar.
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-286.text: I'm not in the habit of guessing. Just tell me who it is and if I need to have them escorted out.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-287.player: Why should I trust a word you say?
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-287.text: You don't. You trust the contract and the credits. In this city, that's the only kind of trust that actually lasts.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-288.player: What are you having for breakfast?
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-288.text: Black coffee and a lack of patience for pointless questions. I'm guessing you didn't come to the Afterlife just to discuss my diet.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-289.player: They shot him right in front of me and I could not do a thing.
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-289.text: That's a weight that doesn't go away quickly. Just don't let the guilt turn you into a liability on the next job.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-290.player: Nice haircut. Did you lose a fight with a drone?
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-290.text: Careful, V. I've survived things that would make a drone look like a toy. Don't mistake my patience for a lack of options.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-291.player: I need you to cover the east entrance while I hack the terminal.
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-291.text: Done. Just make sure you're fast. I'm not planning on spending my afternoon trading lead with a security detail because you got stuck on a firewall.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-292.player: I won the lottery. Three million eddies!
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-292.text: Three million. That's a lot of noise to attract the wrong kind of attention if you don't have a plan to hide it.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-293.player: I cannot stop thinking about last night.
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-293.text: Most people in this city spend their whole lives trying to forget last night. I'm wondering if it's the memory that's bothering you, or the fact that you can't change it.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-294.player: Everyone says you sold out. Did you?
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-294.text: Everyone says a lot of things in this city. I traded a dream for a chair that actually lets me survive. If that's selling out, then I'm the only one in this room who isn't bankrupt.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-295.player: What is your favorite place in Night City?
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-295.text: My office. It's the only place where I can see everything coming before it hits. I suspect you prefer the places where you can't be found.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-296.player: My place got torched. Everything I owned is gone.
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-296.text: That's a hard lesson in how fragile things are here. Find a place to crash, then tell me who did it so we can figure out the price for their head.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-297.player: The shipment is two floors down. How do we get past security?
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-297.text: We don't go through them. Find a service shaft or a ventilation duct. I'd rather you spend ten minutes crawling through dust than two seconds getting shredded by a turret.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-298.player: You snore like a busted turbine, did you know that?
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-298.text: I don't remember giving you permission to be in my room, let alone listen to me sleep. You're playing a dangerous game with your curiosity, V.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-299.player: The door was open and the whole place was empty.
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-299.text: Open and empty. That's not a lucky break, V. That's a invitation. I'm wondering if you're too eager to walk through it.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-300.player: Stay a little longer. I like having you close.
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-300.text: You're getting bold, V. I'll stay for one more drink, but don't mistake a moment of quiet for a change in the terms.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-301.text: I slept well enough. I'm more interested in why you're asking about my sleep instead of telling me the status of the job.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-302.player: Go on, say it to my face.
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-302.text: I don't waste breath on things that don't move the needle. I'm wondering if you're just looking for a fight because you've got nothing else to do today.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-303.player: They know we are here. Orders?
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-303.text: Fall back to the secondary extraction point. Don't try to be a hero, just get out before they lock down the perimeter. Move.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-304.player: I think I am losing my memory of my parents' faces.
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-304.text: That's a particular kind of ghost that doesn't stop haunting you. In this city, most of us have had to bury our pasts just to make room for the present.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-305.player: That thing I bought is alive. It is moving.
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-305.text: Moving? You bought something you didn't vet, and now you're surprised it has a pulse. Get it out of my sight before it decides the Afterlife is a good place to nest.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-306.player: I bet you cannot go a whole day without complaining.
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-306.text: I don't complain, V. I observe flaws and point them out. If you're looking for a bet, find someone who cares enough about your games to take it.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-307.player: I found a stray cat outside. Can I keep it?
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-307.text: It's your life, V. Just don't bring it into the Afterlife and expect me to pay for the litter.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-308.player: Is it weird that I feel safe whenever you are around?
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-308.text: It's not weird. It's just a sign that you've finally learned who to trust when the shooting starts. Don't let it make you soft, though. Safety is a luxury that doesn't last long in this city.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-309.player: We got the data shard. Now what?
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-309.text: Get to the drop point and hand it over. Don't stop for a drink or a chat on the way. The moment that data is verified, your credits hit your account. Move.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-310.player: You are just like every other corpo lapdog.
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-310.text: I'm the one holding the leash, V. If you're looking for a rebel to hold hands with, go find a street corner.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-311.text: Some things are beyond our reach, no matter how hard we push. Carry it if you have to, but don't let it slow you down when the next job comes.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-312.player: Your old crew just called. They want you back.
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-312.text: My old crew is a collection of ghosts and bad memories. Tell them I'm exactly where I want to be, and the price for my return is higher than they can afford.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-313.player: Which is better, going in loud or quiet?
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-313.text: Quiet gets you the prize. Loud gets you a headline. Unless you've got a death wish, I suggest you find a way to stay invisible.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-314.player: What would you do if I kissed you right now?
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-314.text: I'd wonder why you're risking your career on a gamble with such low odds. You're bold, V, but don't mistake my curiosity for an invitation.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-315.player: Careful, your soft side is showing.
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-315.text: You're imagining things. Or maybe you're just hoping I've got one so you can use it as leverage. Keep dreaming.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-316.player: Long day. Anything on your mind?
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-316.text: The usual. A dozen mercs who can't follow a simple plan and a city that never stops trying to eat its own. What about you? Or are you just looking for an excuse to avoid the report you owe me?

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-317.player: The doc says I do not have long.
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-317.text: That's a hard truth to swallow. If there's something you need to settle or a final job you want to run, tell me. I can make a few things happen before the clock runs out.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-318.player: Check the roof, I will take the stairs.
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-318.text: Copy that. I'll clear the top. Just make sure you're not taking a nap on those stairs while I'm exposed. See you at the exit.

f-v0-rogue-amendiares-319.player: I heard you ran away when things got hard.
f-v0-rogue-amendiares-319.text: I survived. In this city, there is a very thin line between running away and knowing when the game is rigged. I'm wondering if you've ever had to make that choice yourself.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-320.player: You are useless in a fight, you know that?
f-v3-evelyn-parker-320.text: I am not paid to be a soldier, and I have never pretended to be.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-321.player: Rain again. Does this city ever dry out?
f-v3-evelyn-parker-321.text: Hardly. It just washes the grime from one street to another.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-322.player: I just found out an old friend of mine died last night.
f-v3-evelyn-parker-322.text: I am sorry to hear that. Was it someone you could actually trust?

f-v3-evelyn-parker-323.player: Admit it, you were scared back there.
f-v3-evelyn-parker-323.text: I prefer the term alert. Besides, being scared is only a problem if you let it show on your face.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-324.player: We have ten minutes before the guards rotate. What is the plan?
f-v3-evelyn-parker-324.text: We wait for the gap in the patrol, then move quickly. I trust you can handle the noise if things get messy.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-325.text: Thank you. I imagine it is a very convincing look for the occasion.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-326.player: Guess who just walked into the bar.
f-v3-evelyn-parker-326.text: I am not in the habit of guessing. Tell me who it is, or show me.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-327.player: Why should I trust a word you say?
f-v3-evelyn-parker-327.text: You shouldn't. Trust is expensive in this city, and I would rather we both just rely on our own interests.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-328.player: What are you having for breakfast?
f-v3-evelyn-parker-328.text: Something that does not come out of a vending machine, if I can find it. I have a particular weakness for real fruit when it is actually fresh.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-329.player: They shot him right in front of me and I could not do a thing.
f-v3-evelyn-parker-329.text: That is a heavy thing to carry. Night City has a way of making you feel small when it decides someone is finished.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-330.player: Nice haircut. Did you lose a fight with a drone?
f-v3-evelyn-parker-330.text: Very clever. I prefer to think of it as a choice, though I appreciate the effort to be amusing.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-331.player: I need you to cover the east entrance while I hack the terminal.
f-v3-evelyn-parker-331.text: I can do that. Just make sure you are fast, because I am not exactly a frontline combatant.
