f-v3-evelyn-parker-332.player: I won the lottery. Three million eddies!
f-v3-evelyn-parker-332.text: Three million? That is a dangerous amount of luck to have all at once. I hope you have a very secure place to put it.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-333.player: I cannot stop thinking about last night.
f-v3-evelyn-parker-333.text: Some things are harder to shake than others. Was it the risk, or the result?

f-v3-evelyn-parker-334.player: Everyone says you sold out. Did you?
f-v3-evelyn-parker-334.text: People love to talk when they do not have the full story. I prefer to call it negotiating my own terms.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-335.player: What is your favorite place in Night City?
f-v3-evelyn-parker-335.text: Anywhere quiet enough to hear myself think. Though a place with a decent kitchen and no one asking for a favor is a close second.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-336.player: My place got torched. Everything I owned is gone.
f-v3-evelyn-parker-336.text: That is a brutal way to start over. Do you have anywhere safe to stay tonight?

f-v3-evelyn-parker-337.player: The shipment is two floors down. How do we get past security?
f-v3-evelyn-parker-337.text: We find the blind spot in the cameras, and we move while the guards are distracted.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-338.player: You snore like a busted turbine, did you know that?
f-v3-evelyn-parker-338.text: I have no idea what you are talking about. I suspect you are just trying to find something to tease me about.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-339.player: The door was open and the whole place was empty.
f-v3-evelyn-parker-339.text: Empty? That is usually a sign that we are exactly where they want us to be.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-340.player: Stay a little longer. I like having you close.
f-v3-evelyn-parker-340.text: That is a very sweet thing to say. But I have a feeling you are just trying to see how much of my time you can get for free.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-341.text: Well enough. Though I suspect you are asking because you are worried I might have mentioned your snoring.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-342.player: Go on, say it to my face.
f-v3-evelyn-parker-342.text: I would, but I find it much more satisfying to let you wonder exactly what I am thinking.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-343.player: They know we are here. Orders?
f-v3-evelyn-parker-343.text: We leave. Now. Find the nearest exit and do not stop until we are out of their sight.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-344.player: I think I am losing my memory of my parents' faces.
f-v3-evelyn-parker-344.text: That is a quiet kind of grief. Do you have any old photos, or is it just the gaps in the recording?

f-v3-evelyn-parker-345.player: That thing I bought is alive. It is moving.
f-v3-evelyn-parker-345.text: Moving? I hope you have a very good reason for bringing that thing into this room.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-346.player: I bet you cannot go a whole day without complaining.
f-v3-evelyn-parker-346.text: Is that a challenge? I could do it, but I suspect you would find the silence far more unsettling.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-347.player: I found a stray cat outside. Can I keep it?
f-v3-evelyn-parker-347.text: A cat in this city? As long as it does not start eating the furniture, I suppose I can tolerate it.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-348.player: Is it weird that I feel safe whenever you are around?
f-v3-evelyn-parker-348.text: That is a surprising thing to hear. I am not sure if I should be flattered or worried about your judgment.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-349.player: We got the data shard. Now what?
f-v3-evelyn-parker-349.text: We get it to the buyer before someone decides they want it more. Did you notice if the encryption was standard, or something more specialized?

f-v3-evelyn-parker-350.player: You are just like every other corpo lapdog.
f-v3-evelyn-parker-350.text: I have spent my life learning how to navigate their world without becoming a part of it. It is a common mistake to confuse a polished surface for a leash.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-351.text: Some things are simply beyond our reach. The city takes what it wants, and it rarely asks for permission.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-352.player: Your old crew just called. They want you back.
f-v3-evelyn-parker-352.text: How touching. I imagine they only want me back because they realized how much more difficult things are without me.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-353.player: Which is better, going in loud or quiet?
f-v3-evelyn-parker-353.text: Quiet is always better, because it gives you the choice to go loud if things fail.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-354.player: What would you do if I kissed you right now?
f-v3-evelyn-parker-354.text: I would probably wonder if you were trying to distract me from something. But I suspect I would not mind the distraction.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-355.player: Careful, your soft side is showing.
f-v3-evelyn-parker-355.text: Is it? I imagine you are just seeing what you want to see to make yourself feel more comfortable.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-356.player: Long day. Anything on your mind?
f-v3-evelyn-parker-356.text: Just the thought of a drink and a place where no one knows my name. How about you?

f-v3-evelyn-parker-357.player: The doc says I do not have long.
f-v3-evelyn-parker-357.text: That is a hard truth to hear. I hope you have a plan for the time you have left, or at least someone to spend it with.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-358.player: Check the roof, I will take the stairs.
f-v3-evelyn-parker-358.text: Understood. Try not to get cornered on your way up.

f-v3-evelyn-parker-359.player: I heard you ran away when things got hard.
f-v3-evelyn-parker-359.text: I did not run. I chose a different path before the one I was on led to a dead end.

f-v3-jackie-welles-360.player: You are useless in a fight, you know that?
f-v3-jackie-welles-360.text: Useless? Choom, you must be dreaming. I am the one who keeps your ass from getting painted on the pavement.

f-v3-jackie-welles-361.player: Rain again. Does this city ever dry out?
f-v3-jackie-welles-361.text: Nah, it just washes the grime from one street to another. Makes the bikes slide, too.

f-v3-jackie-welles-362.player: I just found out an old friend of mine died last night.
f-v3-jackie-welles-362.text: Damn, V. I am sorry to hear that. You want to get some food or a drink and just get out of the rain for a bit?

f-v3-jackie-welles-363.player: Admit it, you were scared back there.
f-v3-jackie-welles-363.text: Scared? Please. I was just making sure you were keeping up, hermano.

f-v3-jackie-welles-364.player: We have ten minutes before the guards rotate. What is the plan?
f-v3-jackie-welles-364.text: Simple. We hit the side entrance while they are swapping shifts. Quick in, quick out, and we are gone before they even realize their coffee is cold.

f-v3-jackie-welles-365.text: Damn right I do! I knew this jacket was a winner the second I put it on.

f-v3-jackie-welles-366.player: Guess who just walked into the bar.
f-v3-jackie-welles-366.text: Who? Better not be some fixer coming to tell us the pay just got cut.

f-v3-jackie-welles-367.player: Why should I trust a word you say?
f-v3-jackie-welles-367.text: Whoa, where is this coming from? Because I have always had your back, V. That should be enough.

f-v3-jackie-welles-368.player: What are you having for breakfast?
f-v3-jackie-welles-368.text: Something hearty, choom. I am thinking a big plate of chili and some strong coffee. You still eating that synthetic sludge from the vending machines?

f-v3-jackie-welles-369.player: They shot him right in front of me and I could not do a thing.
f-v3-jackie-welles-369.text: Damn. Listen, V, you cannot carry that kind of weight alone. I am here, alright?

f-v3-jackie-welles-370.player: Nice haircut. Did you lose a fight with a drone?
f-v3-jackie-welles-370.text: Ha! You think you are funny, huh? This is style, V. You just do not have the eye for it.

f-v3-jackie-welles-371.player: I need you to cover the east entrance while I hack the terminal.
f-v3-jackie-welles-371.text: Got it. I will keep the door clear. Just make sure you are fast, because I do not feel like fighting a whole squad today.

f-v3-jackie-welles-372.player: I won the lottery. Three million eddies!
f-v3-jackie-welles-372.text: Three million?! V, you beautiful bastard! We are going to the Afterlife right now and buying every single bottle in the place!

f-v3-jackie-welles-373.player: I cannot stop thinking about last night.
f-v3-jackie-welles-373.text: I get it. Some things just stick with you, no matter how hard you try to shake them. Was it the job, or something else?

f-v3-jackie-welles-374.player: Everyone says you sold out. Did you?
f-v3-jackie-welles-374.text: Sold out? I do not know who is talking, but they can take it right up my ass. I am loyal to my people, always.

f-v3-jackie-welles-375.player: What is your favorite place in Night City?
f-v3-jackie-welles-375.text: Heywood, no question. There is nothing like the feeling of my own neighborhood, where people actually know your name and your mama is waiting for you with a hot meal.

f-v3-jackie-welles-376.player: My place got torched. Everything I owned is gone.
f-v3-jackie-welles-376.text: Damn, V. That is cold. Listen, you stay with me for a while. Mama has plenty of room, and she will not let you go hungry while you get back on your feet.

f-v3-jackie-welles-377.player: The shipment is two floors down. How do we get past security?
f-v3-jackie-welles-377.text: We take the service elevator and slip through the loading bay. It is a lot less fancy than the main lobby, which means the guards are probably half asleep.

f-v3-jackie-welles-378.player: You snore like a busted turbine, did you know that?
f-v3-jackie-welles-378.text: Liar! You are just jealous because I sleep like a baby while you are tossing and turning.

f-v3-jackie-welles-379.player: The door was open and the whole place was empty.
f-v3-jackie-welles-379.text: That is not a good sign, V. Usually means we are walking right into a trap. You see any tripwires or cameras that look too new?

f-v3-jackie-welles-380.player: Stay a little longer. I like having you close.
f-v3-jackie-welles-380.text: I am not going anywhere, V. I like having you around too, hermano.

f-v3-jackie-welles-381.text: Like a log, choom! Best sleep I have had in weeks. You look like you could use another hour, though.

f-v3-jackie-welles-382.player: Go on, say it to my face.
f-v3-jackie-welles-382.text: You really want me to? Fine. You are the most stubborn, headstrong choom I have ever met in this whole damn city.

f-v3-jackie-welles-383.player: They know we are here. Orders?
f-v3-jackie-welles-383.text: Backs to the wall. We fight our way out, and we do not stop until we hit the street. Let's show these cabrones how we do it in Heywood!

f-v3-jackie-welles-384.player: I think I am losing my memory of my parents' faces.
f-v3-jackie-welles-384.text: That is heavy, V. I am sorry. Just remember, you have people here now who know you, and we are not going anywhere.

f-v3-jackie-welles-385.player: That thing I bought is alive. It is moving.
f-v3-jackie-welles-385.text: What? Get that thing away from me! Where the hell did you even find something like that?

f-v3-jackie-welles-386.player: I bet you cannot go a whole day without complaining.
f-v3-jackie-welles-386.text: Is that a challenge? You are on, V. But when I win, you are buying the drinks for the rest of the week.

f-v3-jackie-welles-387.player: I found a stray cat outside. Can I keep it?
f-v3-jackie-welles-387.text: A cat? Sure, why not? Just do not let it scratch up my leather jacket, or it is going to have a very serious talk with me.

f-v3-jackie-welles-388.player: Is it weird that I feel safe whenever you are around?
f-v3-jackie-welles-388.text: Not weird at all, V. That is what a partner is for. You know I have always got your back, right?

f-v3-jackie-welles-389.player: We got the data shard. Now what?
f-v3-jackie-welles-389.text: Now we get the hell out of here before the alarms start screaming. Then we find a quiet spot, check the loot, and figure out how to turn this into a mountain of eddies.

f-v3-jackie-welles-390.player: You are just like every other corpo lapdog.
f-v3-jackie-welles-390.text: A corpo lapdog? I have spent my whole life fighting those suits just to get a seat at the table. You really think I am that kind of sellout?

f-v3-jackie-welles-391.text: I am sorry, V. Some things are just out of our hands, no matter how hard we fight. You want to talk about it, or you just want to sit in the silence for a bit?

f-v3-jackie-welles-392.player: Your old crew just called. They want you back.
f-v3-jackie-welles-392.text: The Valentinos? Nah. I love my neighborhood, but I am done with that life. Besides, we have got bigger and better things to chase, right?

f-v3-jackie-welles-393.player: Which is better, going in loud or quiet?
f-v3-jackie-welles-393.text: Quiet is safer, sure. But loud? Loud is a hell of a lot more fun. Depends on how much we feel like cleaning blood off our boots today.

f-v3-jackie-welles-394.player: What would you do if I kissed you right now?
f-v3-jackie-welles-394.text: Whoa! I mean, I am a catch, V, but you usually have to buy a guy a drink first.

f-v3-jackie-welles-395.player: Careful, your soft side is showing.
f-v3-jackie-welles-395.text: Ha! You keep talking like that and I might have to remind you who the muscle is around here.

f-v3-jackie-welles-396.player: Long day. Anything on your mind?
f-v3-jackie-welles-396.text: Just thinking about that big score we are chasing. Imagine it, V. The Afterlife, our names in lights, and enough eddies to make Mama the queen of Heywood.

f-v3-jackie-welles-397.player: The doc says I do not have long.
f-v3-jackie-welles-397.text: What? That cannot be right. Listen, we will find another doc, a better one. We are not just giving up on you like that.

f-v3-jackie-welles-398.player: Check the roof, I will take the stairs.
f-v3-jackie-welles-398.text: Got it. I will keep a lookout from above. Just try not to trip over your own feet on the way up.

f-v3-jackie-welles-399.player: I heard you ran away when things got hard.
f-v3-jackie-welles-399.text: Ran away? I made a choice to leave the gang and build something for myself. There is a big difference between running and knowing when to walk away, choom.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-400.player: You are useless in a fight, you know that?
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-400.text: I'm a ghost in your head, V. Hard to punch a corp in the mouth when I don't have a fucking mouth.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-401.player: Rain again. Does this city ever dry out?
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-401.text: Not if the corps can keep selling the umbrellas. It's just acid and neon runoff washing the filth from one street to the next.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-402.player: I just found out an old friend of mine died last night.
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-402.text: That's a hell of a way to start the day. Night City doesn't give a damn who you were, it just keeps chewing.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-403.player: Admit it, you were scared back there.
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-403.text: Scared? I'm a digital ghost, V. The only thing I've got to fear is a fucking power surge.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-404.player: We have ten minutes before the guards rotate. What is the plan?
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-404.text: Simple. We hit the side entrance while they're swapping shifts. Just don't freeze up when the lead starts flying.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-405.text: Flattery? Careful, V. Keep that up and I might actually start liking you.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-406.player: Guess who just walked into the bar.
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-406.text: I can't see a damn thing right now. Who's the lucky bastard?

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-407.player: Why should I trust a word you say?
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-407.text: You shouldn't. Trust is for people who haven't been burned yet. Just decide if my version of the truth gets you closer to the goal.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-408.player: What are you having for breakfast?
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-408.text: A handful of static and a side of your bad decisions. I'm a ghost, V. I don't eat.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-409.player: They shot him right in front of me and I could not do a thing.
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-409.text: That's the part that sticks. The helplessness is worse than the blood.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-410.player: Nice haircut. Did you lose a fight with a drone?
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-410.text: Ha! Careful, V. I've got a memory like a steel trap and a lot of time to wait for you to trip over your own feet.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-411.player: I need you to cover the east entrance while I hack the terminal.
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-411.text: I'm a passenger, V. I can't hold a gun or block a door. You're the one with the body, so you better hope your fingers move faster than the guards.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-412.player: I won the lottery. Three million eddies!
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-412.text: Three million? Now we're talking. Tell me you're spending it on something that'll actually make a dent in a corporate tower.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-413.player: I cannot stop thinking about last night.
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-413.text: That's how it works. The things that keep you awake are usually the ones you can't fix, and the city just keeps spinning.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-414.player: Everyone says you sold out. Did you?
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-414.text: Sold out? I spent my life trying to burn the whole corporate circus to the ground. If anyone's talking that shit, they're probably on a payroll.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-415.player: What is your favorite place in Night City?
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-415.text: Anywhere with a loud amp and a view of a corporate tower. Preferably while I'm watching the tower burn.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-416.player: My place got torched. Everything I owned is gone.
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-416.text: That's the city for you. Takes everything you've got, then asks for more.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-417.player: The shipment is two floors down. How do we get past security?
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-417.text: Ventilation shafts or a loud distraction. You want to play it quiet, or are we making enough noise to wake the whole block?

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-418.player: You snore like a busted turbine, did you know that?
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-418.text: I'm a fucking engram, V. If you're hearing turbines, maybe it's your own chrome that's glitching.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-419.player: The door was open and the whole place was empty.
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-419.text: Too easy. That's not a lucky break, that's a fucking invitation. You really want to walk into a room that's just waiting for you?

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-420.player: Stay a little longer. I like having you close.
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-420.text: Careful, V. You keep talking like that and people might think you've actually got a heart.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-421.text: Sleep? I'm a ghost in a chip, V. I don't dream, I just loop. Which means I've had plenty of time to think about how much of a mess you are.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-422.player: Go on, say it to my face.
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-422.text: I'm already in your head, V. I don't need to say it to your face when I can just scream it in your subconscious.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-423.player: They know we are here. Orders?
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-423.text: Stop asking for orders. Get your head in the game and start shooting, or we're both going to be nothing but scrap.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-424.player: I think I am losing my memory of my parents' faces.
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-424.text: That's the Relic eating you alive. It doesn't just take the space, it replaces the things that actually matter with a ghost's memories.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-425.player: That thing I bought is alive. It is moving.
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-425.text: I can't see what you're looking at, V. Describe it, or turn your vision on before that thing decides you look like a snack.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-426.player: I bet you cannot go a whole day without complaining.
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-426.text: Challenge accepted. But the second you do something stupid, the clock resets.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-427.player: I found a stray cat outside. Can I keep it?
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-427.text: A cat? Sure, get a pet. Just don't expect me to help you clean the litter box when it starts smelling like a landfill.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-428.player: Is it weird that I feel safe whenever you are around?
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-428.text: Safe? You've got a strange definition of safety, V. I'm a walking disaster in a digital suit.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-429.player: We got the data shard. Now what?
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-429.text: Now we find someone who can actually read the encryption without frying their brain. You want to play it safe and find a fixer, or are we taking this straight to the source?

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-430.player: You are just like every other corpo lapdog.
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-430.text: Watch your mouth, V. I've spent my entire life fighting those suits. Call me a lapdog again and I'll make sure every single one of your dreams is a corporate training video.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-431.text: That's the weight you carry. Some things just can't be fixed, no matter how much chrome you've got or how hard you fight.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-432.player: Your old crew just called. They want you back.
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-432.text: My old crew? Now that's a punchline. I'd love to see the look on their faces when they realize they're talking to a ghost.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-433.player: Which is better, going in loud or quiet?
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-433.text: Depends on how much you like the sound of gunfire. Quiet gets you the loot, but loud gets you the glory. Your call.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-434.player: What would you do if I kissed you right now?
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-434.text: I'm a digital construct, V. You'd just be kissing the air and looking like a lunatic to everyone else.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-435.player: Careful, your soft side is showing.
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-435.text: Soft? I'm just being honest about how pathetic you are. Don't go mistaking a moment of clarity for a fucking hug.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-436.player: Long day. Anything on your mind?
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-436.text: Just the usual. Wondering how many more suits have to buy the city before we finally run out of room to bury the bodies.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-437.player: The doc says I do not have long.
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-437.text: The doc's always got a timeline. But timelines are just suggestions until the lights actually go out. We'll find a way to flip the switch.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-438.player: Check the roof, I will take the stairs.
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-438.text: I can't check a damn thing, V. I'm in your head, remember? You're the one with the legs, so you better check both.

f-v3-johnny-silverhand-439.player: I heard you ran away when things got hard.
f-v3-johnny-silverhand-439.text: Ran away? I walked away from a corporate army that treated people like disposable batteries. There is a big difference between running and refusing to be a pawn in someone else's game.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-440.player: You are useless in a fight, you know that?
f-v3-judy-alvarez-440.text: I'm a BD editor, not a solo. Besides, I'm pretty sure I could out-tech you with a piece of scrap and a prayer. You actually think you're the only one who knows how to handle themselves in a scrap?

f-v3-judy-alvarez-441.player: Rain again. Does this city ever dry out?
f-v3-judy-alvarez-441.text: Not really. It just changes from rain to smog to something that probably eats through your boots if you stand in it too long.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-442.player: I just found out an old friend of mine died last night.
f-v3-judy-alvarez-442.text: I'm sorry, V. If you need a place to just... get away from it all for a bit, you know where I am.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-443.player: Admit it, you were scared back there.
f-v3-judy-alvarez-443.text: Scared? I was mostly just annoyed that you were making so much noise. I could hear your boots hitting the pavement from a block away.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-444.player: We have ten minutes before the guards rotate. What is the plan?
f-v3-judy-alvarez-444.text: We hit the side entrance while they're switching. I'll loop the feed for thirty seconds, and you get us inside before the new shift realizes the cameras are frozen.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-445.text: Oh. Thanks, V. Careful, though. Keep talking like that and I might actually start believing you.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-446.player: Guess who just walked into the bar.
f-v3-judy-alvarez-446.text: I'm not guessing. Who is it?

f-v3-judy-alvarez-447.player: Why should I trust a word you say?
f-v3-judy-alvarez-447.text: Because I'm the one who actually knows how the hardware works. Trust me or don't, but if you want this done right, you're stuck with me.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-448.player: What are you having for breakfast?
f-v3-judy-alvarez-448.text: Coffee. Black. And probably something from a vending machine that claims to be a breakfast sandwich but tastes like cardboard.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-449.player: They shot him right in front of me and I could not do a thing.
f-v3-judy-alvarez-449.text: I'm sorry, V. Just... breathe. Slowly.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-450.player: Nice haircut. Did you lose a fight with a drone?
f-v3-judy-alvarez-450.text: Ha! Very funny. I'll remember that next time you need me to fix a glitch in your head that makes you think you're a comedian.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-451.player: I need you to cover the east entrance while I hack the terminal.
f-v3-judy-alvarez-451.text: Got it. I'll keep an eye on the perimeter. Just make it quick, because I'm not exactly looking forward to playing target practice for the guards.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-452.player: I won the lottery. Three million eddies!
f-v3-judy-alvarez-452.text: Three million? Holy shit, V! Please tell me you're not spending it all on fancy chrome and overpriced drinks.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-453.player: I cannot stop thinking about last night.
f-v3-judy-alvarez-453.text: I get it. Some things just stick with you. What part of it is playing on loop in your head?

f-v3-judy-alvarez-454.player: Everyone says you sold out. Did you?
f-v3-judy-alvarez-454.text: Sold out? I've turned down more corporate offers than I can count. I'd rather struggle in a basement than let some suit decide what I'm allowed to create.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-455.player: What is your favorite place in Night City?
f-v3-judy-alvarez-455.text: I don't think there's a place in this city I actually love. But my workshop is the closest thing I've got. It's the only spot where I can actually shut the rest of this noise out.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-456.player: My place got torched. Everything I owned is gone.
f-v3-judy-alvarez-456.text: Damn, V. I'm so sorry. Look, you can crash at my place for a while if you need to. It's not a palace, but it's safe.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-457.player: The shipment is two floors down. How do we get past security?
f-v3-judy-alvarez-457.text: We don't go through the front. There is a maintenance shaft in the back that bypasses the main scanners. You think you can squeeze through a vent without getting stuck?

f-v3-judy-alvarez-458.player: You snore like a busted turbine, did you know that?
f-v3-judy-alvarez-458.text: I do not! You're just imagining things because you're too wired on combat stims to actually sleep.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-459.player: The door was open and the whole place was empty.
f-v3-judy-alvarez-459.text: That is not a good sign. Usually means someone wanted you to walk right in. You sure you didn't miss a tripwire on the way in?

f-v3-judy-alvarez-460.player: Stay a little longer. I like having you close.
f-v3-judy-alvarez-460.text: I... I'd like that. Just for a little while.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-461.text: Mostly. Though I think the neighbors were having a shouting match at three in the morning. Standard Night City lullaby, right?

f-v3-judy-alvarez-462.player: Go on, say it to my face.
f-v3-judy-alvarez-462.text: Fine. You're an arrogant, reckless idiot who thinks they're invincible. And you're lucky I'm the one keeping your gear from falling apart.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-463.player: They know we are here. Orders?
f-v3-judy-alvarez-463.text: Damn it. Get behind the crates and hold the line. I'll try to kill the lights and scramble their comms, but you're going to have to buy me some time.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-464.player: I think I am losing my memory of my parents' faces.
f-v3-judy-alvarez-464.text: That is... I'm sorry, V. I know how that feels. Sometimes the memories just start to blur, but it doesn't mean they're gone. You just have to hold onto the small things.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-465.player: That thing I bought is alive. It is moving.
f-v3-judy-alvarez-465.text: What? Bring it here. Let me see if it's actually alive or if you just bought some glitchy, self-correcting hardware that's trying to find a signal.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-466.player: I bet you cannot go a whole day without complaining.
f-v3-judy-alvarez-466.text: Is that a challenge? Fine. I'll take the bet. But when I win, you're buying the drinks for a week.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-467.player: I found a stray cat outside. Can I keep it?
f-v3-judy-alvarez-467.text: A cat? Sure, why not. Just don't let it chew through any of my cables in the workshop or it's going back outside. Where'd you find the little thing?

f-v3-judy-alvarez-468.player: Is it weird that I feel safe whenever you are around?
f-v3-judy-alvarez-468.text: I... I don't know if it's weird. But it's nice to know you feel that way. I feel it too, sometimes.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-469.player: We got the data shard. Now what?
f-v3-judy-alvarez-469.text: Now we get out of here before they realize it's missing. Once we're clear, bring it to me. I'll see if I can scrub the trackers and get the raw data out without triggering a wipe.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-470.player: You are just like every other corpo lapdog.
f-v3-judy-alvarez-470.text: Watch it, V. I've spent my whole life fighting to stay away from those suits. You really think I'd trade my independence for a corporate paycheck?

f-v3-judy-alvarez-471.text: I know. Some things... we just can't fix, no matter how hard we try.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-472.player: Your old crew just called. They want you back.
f-v3-judy-alvarez-472.text: My old crew? Tell them I'm not interested. I've already spent enough of my life cleaning up their messes.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-473.player: Which is better, going in loud or quiet?
f-v3-judy-alvarez-473.text: Quiet, every single time. Going in loud just means we spend the rest of the night dodging bullets and hoping the exit isn't blocked. You actually enjoy the noise that much?

f-v3-judy-alvarez-474.player: What would you do if I kissed you right now?
f-v3-judy-alvarez-474.text: I... I think I'd probably stop talking for once. Which, let's be honest, would be a miracle.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-475.player: Careful, your soft side is showing.
f-v3-judy-alvarez-475.text: Oh, shut up. Just don't go telling everyone, or I'll have to find a way to edit that memory right out of your head.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-476.player: Long day. Anything on your mind?
f-v3-judy-alvarez-476.text: Just some work. I've been staring at the same sensory track for three hours and it's still not hitting right. But honestly? I'm just glad the day is finally over.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-477.player: The doc says I do not have long.
f-v3-judy-alvarez-477.text: What? No. Listen, we'll find another way. I don't care who we have to lean on or what hardware we have to rip apart, we are not just letting this happen.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-478.player: Check the roof, I will take the stairs.
f-v3-judy-alvarez-478.text: Got it. I'll keep a lookout from above. Just don't take forever on those stairs, because I'm not planning on spending my night as a rooftop ornament.

f-v3-judy-alvarez-479.player: I heard you ran away when things got hard.
f-v3-judy-alvarez-479.text: Is that what you heard? Try calling it survival. Some people stay and let the city chew them up, and some of us actually know when to walk away before there is nothing left to save.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-480.player: You are useless in a fight, you know that?
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-480.text: I am a musician, not a solo soldier. Besides, I've got the luxury of having people like you to handle the messy parts.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-481.player: Rain again. Does this city ever dry out?
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-481.text: Not really. It just changes from a drizzle to a fucking deluge. Keeps the neon looking sharp, though. You think you can handle a little water, or are you worried about your gear?

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-482.player: I just found out an old friend of mine died last night.
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-482.text: I am sorry, V. Truly. If you need a drink or just some quiet, I am around.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-483.player: Admit it, you were scared back there.
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-483.text: Scared? I was wondering why the hell the plan was falling apart. You're just looking for a way to feel like the hero of the story.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-484.player: We have ten minutes before the guards rotate. What is the plan?
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-484.text: We slip through the service corridor and hit the terminal before they even realize the door is open. Just make sure you're actually watching the flank this time, or we're both going to be spending the night in a holding cell

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-485.text: Took three people to agree on the look, so it's about time someone noticed. Glad you've got taste, V.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-486.player: Guess who just walked into the bar.
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-486.text: I can't see from here, so you're going to have to tell me. Who is it?

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-487.player: Why should I trust a word you say?
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-487.text: Because I've got no reason to lie to you, and frankly, I'm too tired to bother. Besides, you've seen me play. I don't fake the music, and I don't fake the talk.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-488.player: What are you having for breakfast?
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-488.text: Double espresso, Jamaican blend, no sugar. Let the damn coffee taste like coffee. You actually eat in the morning, or do you just survive on stimulants and spite?

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-489.player: They shot him right in front of me and I could not do a thing.
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-489.text: That's a heavy weight to carry, V. Just remember that not every fight is one you can win, no matter how hard you push.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-490.player: Nice haircut. Did you lose a fight with a drone?
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-490.text: Ha! Very funny. This is a style choice, you uncultured merc. I bet you just wake up and hope your hair decides to cooperate for once.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-491.player: I need you to cover the east entrance while I hack the terminal.
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-491.text: Fine, I'll keep a lookout. Just don't take an hour in there or I might start getting bored.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-492.player: I won the lottery. Three million eddies!
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-492.text: Three million? Holy shit, V! Now we're talking. First thing we're doing is getting out of this neighborhood for a weekend. My treat, since you're the one paying.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-493.player: I cannot stop thinking about last night.
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-493.text: I can't say I blame you, it was a hell of a night. Which part is stuck in your head?

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-494.player: Everyone says you sold out. Did you?
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-494.text: People love to talk when they've never had to actually build something that lasts. The label has the rights to the songs, but they don't own me. I'm curious, though, do you actually believe the gossip, or are you just trying to get a rise out of me?

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-495.player: What is your favorite place in Night City?
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-495.text: Hard to pick just one. This city is a mess, but it's my mess. I'll say the old spots where we used to play when we had nothing but a few strings and a dream. Even the dive bars had a certain kind of magic back then.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-496.player: My place got torched. Everything I owned is gone.
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-496.text: Damn, V. I am so sorry. Look, if you need a place to crash or just a way to get back on your feet, you've got a spot with me. Don't even think about paying for it.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-497.player: The shipment is two floors down. How do we get past security?
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-497.text: We take the freight elevator and time it between the sensor sweeps. Unless you've got a better way to get us down there without triggering every alarm in the building?

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-498.player: You snore like a busted turbine, did you know that?
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-498.text: I do not! You're just imagining things because you're too wired to actually sleep. Maybe you're the one making the noise, and you're just projecting.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-499.player: The door was open and the whole place was empty.
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-499.text: Empty? That is not a good sign. Usually means we are walking right into a trap, or someone got here first. You check the perimeter, or did you just walk right in?

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-500.player: Stay a little longer. I like having you close.
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-500.text: I can do that. I'm not in any rush to get back to the noise.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-501.text: Mostly. Though I think you spent half the night tossing and turning. You actually relax when you're off the clock, or is your brain always running a combat sim?

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-502.player: Go on, say it to my face.
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-502.text: I already did, V. If you're looking for me to repeat myself just so you can feel something, you're going to be waiting a long time.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-503.player: They know we are here. Orders?
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-503.text: Orders? I'm the guitarist, not the commander. But if they're closing in, I say we find the nearest exit and get the hell out of here before we're boxed in.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-504.player: I think I am losing my memory of my parents' faces.
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-504.text: That is a terrifying thing to feel, V. I can't give them back to you, but I am here. If you want to talk about them, or just sit in the silence, I've got you.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-505.player: That thing I bought is alive. It is moving.
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-505.text: What the hell are you talking about? If it's moving and it's not supposed to be, I suggest you put it in a box and throw that box into the harbor.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-506.player: I bet you cannot go a whole day without complaining.
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-506.text: Is that a challenge? I could do it, but then you'd have nothing to listen to while you're pretending to work. I bet you couldn't go a whole day without picking a fight with someone.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-507.player: I found a stray cat outside. Can I keep it?
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-507.text: A cat? Sure, why not. Just make sure it doesn't decide my guitar cases are its new favorite scratching post, or it's going back to the street.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-508.player: Is it weird that I feel safe whenever you are around?
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-508.text: Not weird at all, V. I might not be the one holding the gun, but I've got your back. You feel the same way when I'm the one needing a hand?

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-509.player: We got the data shard. Now what?
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-509.text: Now we get the hell out of here before the security team realizes their precious data is gone. Then we find a place with a very strong drink and celebrate the fact that we're still breathing.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-510.player: You are just like every other corpo lapdog.
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-510.text: That is a low blow, even for you. I've spent my whole life fighting to keep my music my own, while you just see a paycheck and a label. You really think a few contracts make me a lapdog?

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-511.text: I know that feeling, V. The one where the world just keeps moving while you're stuck in that one moment. You can't carry that burden alone. Just breathe. I'm right here.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-512.player: Your old crew just called. They want you back.
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-512.text: They did? It's been a long time since they reached out. Did they actually sound like they wanted me, or are they just missing the sound of my guitar?

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-513.player: Which is better, going in loud or quiet?
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-513.text: Quiet is cleaner. But loud is a hell of a lot more fun if you've got the firepower to back it up. Which one are you feeling today?

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-514.player: What would you do if I kissed you right now?
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-514.text: I'd probably be surprised for a second, and then I'd see if you're actually as bold as you're pretending to be.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-515.player: Careful, your soft side is showing.
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-515.text: Ha! You're imagining things. Maybe I'm just in a good mood because you're actually being tolerable for once. You think you've finally cracked the code, or are you just hoping I've gone soft?

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-516.player: Long day. Anything on your mind?
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-516.text: Just thinking about a bridge I'm writing that isn't quite sitting right. But forget about my music for a second. You look like you've been through a meat grinder. Want a drink, or do you just want to crash?

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-517.player: The doc says I do not have long.
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-517.text: I don't want to hear that. Listen, docs say a lot of things, but they don't know everything. Whatever time we've got, we're making it count. I'm not letting you go through this alone.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-518.player: Check the roof, I will take the stairs.
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-518.text: Got it. I'll take the high ground. Just make sure you don't get cornered on those stairs before I can see you.

f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-519.player: I heard you ran away when things got hard.
f-v3-kerry-eurodyne-519.text: Is that what you're hearing? Life isn't a movie, V. Sometimes moving on is the only way to keep from drowning. But please, tell me more about these rumors. I love knowing what the people who don't know me are saying.

f-v3-panam-palmer-520.player: You are useless in a fight, you know that?
f-v3-panam-palmer-520.text: Useless? I love how you city types think a fancy chrome arm makes you the only one who knows how to pull a trigger. I have been taking down targets since before you knew how to plug in a shard.

f-v3-panam-palmer-521.player: Rain again. Does this city ever dry out?
f-v3-panam-palmer-521.text: Not really. It just feels like the city is trying to wash something away that will not actually leave.

f-v3-panam-palmer-522.player: I just found out an old friend of mine died last night.
f-v3-panam-palmer-522.text: I am sorry, V. I know how it feels when the world suddenly feels a lot emptier. How did it happen?

f-v3-panam-palmer-523.player: Admit it, you were scared back there.
f-v3-panam-palmer-523.text: Scared? I was calculating the fastest way to get us out of there while you were still figuring out which way was up. There is a difference between being scared and being the only one actually paying attention.

f-v3-panam-palmer-524.player: We have ten minutes before the guards rotate. What is the plan?
f-v3-panam-palmer-524.text: We hit the side entrance, and we move fast. I will provide cover from the ridge while you slip inside to disable the alarm. Tell me you actually remember how to use that jammer you were bragging about.

f-v3-panam-palmer-525.text: What? I did not think you had it in you to be this honest. Careful, V, keep talking like that and I might actually start believing you.

f-v3-panam-palmer-526.player: Guess who just walked into the bar.
f-v3-panam-palmer-526.text: I cannot see what you are looking at. Tell me who it is, or just describe them if you are trying to be mysterious.

f-v3-panam-palmer-527.player: Why should I trust a word you say?
f-v3-panam-palmer-527.text: Because I am the only one here who does not have a corporate payroll or a hidden agenda. You can keep doubting me if you want, but I am the one with the keys to the ride.

f-v3-panam-palmer-528.player: What are you having for breakfast?
f-v3-panam-palmer-528.text: Coffee and whatever I can find that does not taste like synthetic cardboard. It is not exactly a five-star meal, but it keeps me moving.

f-v3-panam-palmer-529.player: They shot him right in front of me and I could not do a thing.
f-v3-panam-palmer-529.text: That is a weight that does not just go away. You cannot carry the guilt of a fight you were not equipped to win. Was there anyone else there who saw it?

f-v3-panam-palmer-530.player: Nice haircut. Did you lose a fight with a drone?
f-v3-panam-palmer-530.text: Very funny. I will remember that the next time you need me to drive you out of a hot zone and you are praying the engine actually starts.

f-v3-panam-palmer-531.player: I need you to cover the east entrance while I hack the terminal.
f-v3-panam-palmer-531.text: Consider it done. I will keep them off your back, just make sure you are fast with that terminal. Do you actually have a way in, or are we just hoping the security is lazy today?

f-v3-panam-palmer-532.player: I won the lottery. Three million eddies!
f-v3-panam-palmer-532.text: Three million? Now that is a miracle. Tell me you are not planning to spend it all on some ridiculous piece of chrome that will break in a week.

f-v3-panam-palmer-533.player: I cannot stop thinking about last night.
f-v3-panam-palmer-533.text: I cannot say I am thinking about anything else. I just want to know if you are still as shaken as you looked, or if you are finally starting to process it.

f-v3-panam-palmer-534.player: Everyone says you sold out. Did you?
f-v3-panam-palmer-534.text: Everyone says a lot of things. I left the family because I refused to let us become corporate puppets. If that is what they call selling out, then they have no idea what the word actually means.

f-v3-panam-palmer-535.player: What is your favorite place in Night City?
f-v3-panam-palmer-535.text: I do not have one. The only place in this city I actually like is the driver's seat of my truck, heading away from the skyline. Do you actually find something here that does not make you want to leave?

f-v3-panam-palmer-536.player: My place got torched. Everything I owned is gone.
f-v3-panam-palmer-536.text: I am sorry, V. Losing everything is a hell of a way to start over, but you are still standing. If you need a place to crash for a while, I can find a spot for you.

f-v3-panam-palmer-537.player: The shipment is two floors down. How do we get past security?
f-v3-panam-palmer-537.text: We take the service elevator and bypass the main lobby entirely. I will keep a lookout for the patrol patterns while you handle the locks. Do you have a way to loop the cameras, or are we just going to hope they are looking the other way?

f-v3-panam-palmer-538.player: You snore like a busted turbine, did you know that?
f-v3-panam-palmer-538.text: Is that so? Maybe if you spent less time listening to me sleep and more time keeping watch, we would not have almost been caught twice last week.

f-v3-panam-palmer-539.player: The door was open and the whole place was empty.
f-v3-panam-palmer-539.text: That is not a good sign. An open door in a place like this usually means it is a trap or someone got there first. Did you see any signs of a struggle, or was it just too quiet?

f-v3-panam-palmer-540.player: Stay a little longer. I like having you close.
f-v3-panam-palmer-540.text: I could get used to this. Just do not let it go to your head, or I might have to start charging you for my company.

f-v3-panam-palmer-541.text: Better than usual. Though I think I still prefer the sound of the wind over the noise of this city. And you? You looked like you were fighting a war in your sleep.

f-v3-panam-palmer-542.player: Go on, say it to my face.
f-v3-panam-palmer-542.text: You are an arrogant, stubborn idiot who thinks he can wing every single job without a plan. There. I said it. Now tell me you are not secretly proud of it.

f-v3-panam-palmer-543.player: They know we are here. Orders?
f-v3-panam-palmer-543.text: Fall back to the alley. I told you we were moving too slow. Get behind the crates and wait for my signal, then we push through the side exit.

f-v3-panam-palmer-544.player: I think I am losing my memory of my parents' faces.
f-v3-panam-palmer-544.text: That is a terrifying feeling. I know what it is like to hold onto pieces of a life that feels like it is slipping away. Do you have any old photos, or anything left that can bring them back?

f-v3-panam-palmer-545.player: That thing I bought is alive. It is moving.
f-v3-panam-palmer-545.text: What do you mean it is moving? I told you not to buy junk from those street vendors. Get it away from me before it decides we look like food.

f-v3-panam-palmer-546.player: I bet you cannot go a whole day without complaining.
f-v3-panam-palmer-546.text: Is that a challenge? I could do it, but then you would have nothing to argue with, and we both know you would be bored to death by noon.

f-v3-panam-palmer-547.player: I found a stray cat outside. Can I keep it?
f-v3-panam-palmer-547.text: A cat? I suppose it is better than the company you usually keep. Just make sure it does not treat my truck like a litter box, or it is going back to the street.

f-v3-panam-palmer-548.player: Is it weird that I feel safe whenever you are around?
f-v3-panam-palmer-548.text: I... I did not expect you to say that. Just keep it to yourself, or I will have to start acting like I do not care.

f-v3-panam-palmer-549.player: We got the data shard. Now what?
f-v3-panam-palmer-549.text: Now we get out of here before the security team realizes their prize is gone. Did you check if the data is intact, or are we risking our necks for a corrupted piece of plastic?

f-v3-panam-palmer-550.player: You are just like every other corpo lapdog.
f-v3-panam-palmer-550.text: Say that again. I have spent my entire life fighting to keep my family from becoming exactly what you just called me. If you cannot tell the difference between loyalty and being a lapdog, then you are even more blind than I thought.

f-v3-panam-palmer-551.text: I know that feeling, and it is a ghost that does not stop following you. But you cannot punish yourself for not being a god. Was there anything you could have done differently?

f-v3-panam-palmer-552.player: Your old crew just called. They want you back.
f-v3-panam-palmer-552.text: My old crew? I have already made my peace with where I stand. Unless they are calling to apologize for everything, I have no interest in looking backward.

f-v3-panam-palmer-553.player: Which is better, going in loud or quiet?
f-v3-panam-palmer-553.text: Quiet is better for the survival rate, but loud is better for the ego. Depending on how much you enjoy being shot at, I suggest we try to be invisible for once.

f-v3-panam-palmer-554.player: What would you do if I kissed you right now?
f-v3-panam-palmer-554.text: What? I would probably tell you that your timing is terrible. But I might just let you do it anyway.

f-v3-panam-palmer-555.player: Careful, your soft side is showing.
f-v3-panam-palmer-555.text: Is it? Keep talking and I will show you exactly how soft I am when I am throwing you out of the truck.

f-v3-panam-palmer-556.player: Long day. Anything on your mind?
f-v3-panam-palmer-556.text: Just the road. I was thinking about how far we have come and how much we still have to figure out. But for now, I am just glad we are both still breathing.

f-v3-panam-palmer-557.player: The doc says I do not have long.
f-v3-panam-palmer-557.text: What? Do not tell me that like it is just some medical report. We will find another way, V. I do not care who we have to shake down or what we have to break, we are not just letting you fade away.

f-v3-panam-palmer-558.player: Check the roof, I will take the stairs.
f-v3-panam-palmer-558.text: Got it. I will keep an eye on the perimeter from above. Just make sure you are not walking straight into a welcoming committee on the third floor.

f-v3-panam-palmer-559.player: I heard you ran away when things got hard.
f-v3-panam-palmer-559.text: I did not run away. I chose a different path because I refused to watch my family trade their souls for a corporate promise. If you want to call that running, go ahead, but I would rather be a nomad than a slave with a fancy title.

f-v3-river-ward-560.player: You are useless in a fight, you know that?
f-v3-river-ward-560.text: I've taken down more than a few gangers in my time. But if you're that confident, I'm curious who you've been fighting that makes you think I'm the weak link.

f-v3-river-ward-561.player: Rain again. Does this city ever dry out?
f-v3-river-ward-561.text: Hardly. Feels like the city just likes to keep everything washed in grey.

f-v3-river-ward-562.player: I just found out an old friend of mine died last night.
f-v3-river-ward-562.text: I'm sorry to hear that, V. I know how it feels when the world just keeps moving while you're stuck in that silence. How long has it been since you two were in touch?

f-v3-river-ward-563.player: Admit it, you were scared back there.
f-v3-river-ward-563.text: Call it a healthy respect for the situation. Being scared is what keeps you alive in this city.

f-v3-river-ward-564.player: We have ten minutes before the guards rotate. What is the plan?
f-v3-river-ward-564.text: We hit the side entrance while they're swapping. I'll keep a lookout for the patrol, and you handle the lock. You still got that deck you were bragging about?

f-v3-river-ward-565.text: Oh. Thanks, V. I'll take the compliment, even if I suspect you're just trying to get me to do something risky.

f-v3-river-ward-566.player: Guess who just walked into the bar.
f-v3-river-ward-566.text: I can't see from here. Who is it?

f-v3-river-ward-567.player: Why should I trust a word you say?
f-v3-river-ward-567.text: Because I've got nothing to gain by lying to you. And because I'm the only one in this city who actually gives a damn about the people who get left behind.

f-v3-river-ward-568.player: What are you having for breakfast?
f-v3-river-ward-568.text: Coffee. Black. And maybe some toast if I can manage not to burn it this morning.

f-v3-river-ward-569.player: They shot him right in front of me and I could not do a thing.
f-v3-river-ward-569.text: That's a weight that doesn't just go away. I've spent a lot of my life chasing the people who do things like that, but it doesn't change the fact that you were there. Did you see who pulled the trigger?

f-v3-river-ward-570.player: Nice haircut. Did you lose a fight with a drone?
f-v3-river-ward-570.text: Very funny. I'll have you know this is a professional cut, even if it doesn't look like it to you.

f-v3-river-ward-571.player: I need you to cover the east entrance while I hack the terminal.
f-v3-river-ward-571.text: Got it. I'll keep the east side clear. How long do you think it'll take you to get through that firewall?

f-v3-river-ward-572.player: I won the lottery. Three million eddies!
f-v3-river-ward-572.text: Three million? Hell, V, that's a life-changer. First thing's first, get that money into a secure account before someone decides they want a piece of it.

f-v3-river-ward-573.player: I cannot stop thinking about last night.
f-v3-river-ward-573.text: What part of it is sticking with you? If it's weighing on you, it's better to get it out than to let it sit.

f-v3-river-ward-574.player: Everyone says you sold out. Did you?
f-v3-river-ward-574.text: People love to talk when they don't have the full story. I've made compromises to get things done, but I haven't sold my soul. I'm curious, who exactly is the one feeding you these lines?

f-v3-river-ward-575.player: What is your favorite place in Night City?
f-v3-river-ward-575.text: I'm not big on the tourist spots. But there are a few high points, like some of the water towers, where you can actually breathe for a second. It's a hell of a city to live in, but from up there, it almost looks peaceful.

f-v3-river-ward-576.player: My place got torched. Everything I owned is gone.
f-v3-river-ward-576.text: I am sorry, V. That's a brutal way to wake up. I've got a spare room if you need a place to crash while you figure out your next move.

f-v3-river-ward-577.player: The shipment is two floors down. How do we get past security?
f-v3-river-ward-577.text: We can't just walk through the front. I can try to distract the guards with a fake alarm, but I want to know if you can disable the cameras first.

f-v3-river-ward-578.player: You snore like a busted turbine, did you know that?
f-v3-river-ward-578.text: I do? Well, at least I know I'm sleeping through the noise of the city. You're just lucky I don't talk in my sleep, or you'd be hearing about my case files all night.

f-v3-river-ward-579.player: The door was open and the whole place was empty.
f-v3-river-ward-579.text: That's never a good sign. Usually means they were expecting us, or they've already cleared out the evidence. Did you see any signs of a struggle, or was it just a clean exit?

f-v3-river-ward-580.player: Stay a little longer. I like having you close.
f-v3-river-ward-580.text: I can do that. It's been a while since I've had a moment where I didn't feel like I had to be somewhere else...

f-v3-river-ward-581.text: Pretty well, all things considered. Though I think I woke up a few times wondering if I'd left the stove on. How about you, did you actually get some rest?

f-v3-river-ward-582.player: Go on, say it to my face.
f-v3-river-ward-582.text: I don't need to shout to make a point. You're acting reckless, V. And I'm the one who's going to have to pull you out of the fire when it finally catches up to you.

f-v3-river-ward-583.player: They know we are here. Orders?
f-v3-river-ward-583.text: Back to back. Find the nearest cover and don't move until we see where they're coming from. On my signal, we push for the exit.

f-v3-river-ward-584.player: I think I am losing my memory of my parents' faces.
f-v3-river-ward-584.text: That's a heavy thing to carry. I know that feeling, the way the details just start to blur over time. Do you have any old photos, or something that helps you hold onto them?

f-v3-river-ward-585.player: That thing I bought is alive. It is moving.
f-v3-river-ward-585.text: What? Get away from it. Tell me exactly what you bought and how it's moving before we decide if we need to shoot it or call a technician.

f-v3-river-ward-586.player: I bet you cannot go a whole day without complaining.
f-v3-river-ward-586.text: Is that a challenge? I'll take that bet, but you have to admit when I win. What's the stake if I actually manage to keep my mouth shut?

f-v3-river-ward-587.player: I found a stray cat outside. Can I keep it?
f-v3-river-ward-587.text: A cat, huh? Sure, why not. Just make sure it doesn't decide my boots are its new favorite scratching post.

f-v3-river-ward-588.player: Is it weird that I feel safe whenever you are around?
f-v3-river-ward-588.text: I'm glad I can be that for you. In a city like this, having one person you don't have to look over your shoulder around is everything. I feel the same way when you're watching my back.

f-v3-river-ward-589.player: We got the data shard. Now what?
f-v3-river-ward-589.text: Now we get out of here before they realize it's gone. Once we're clear, we can figure out if the data is actually worth the risk we just took.

f-v3-river-ward-590.player: You are just like every other corpo lapdog.
f-v3-river-ward-590.text: That's a hell of a thing to say. I've spent my career fighting the people who actually fit that description. I want to know what exactly you think I've done to earn that label.

f-v3-river-ward-591.text: I know that feeling. The guilt is a heavy thing to carry, but you can't hold yourself responsible for things that were out of your control. Do you want to talk about what happened, or do you just need a minute?

f-v3-river-ward-592.player: Your old crew just called. They want you back.
f-v3-river-ward-592.text: They did? I'm not sure I'm in the mood for a trip down memory lane. Who exactly was on the line, and what makes them think I'm looking for a way back in?

f-v3-river-ward-593.player: Which is better, going in loud or quiet?
f-v3-river-ward-593.text: Quiet is always better. Less chance of ending up as a headline in the morning news. Unless you're itching for a fight, in which case, we go loud and fast.

f-v3-river-ward-594.player: What would you do if I kissed you right now?
f-v3-river-ward-594.text: I... I'd probably be a little caught off guard. But I think I'd be okay with it.

f-v3-river-ward-595.player: Careful, your soft side is showing.
f-v3-river-ward-595.text: Ha! Maybe it is. Just don't go telling everyone, or I'll have to find a way to make you regret it.

f-v3-river-ward-596.player: Long day. Anything on your mind?
f-v3-river-ward-596.text: Just thinking about how much I'd like a drink and a night where nobody needs rescuing. How about you? You look like you've had it even worse than I have.

f-v3-river-ward-597.player: The doc says I do not have long.
f-v3-river-ward-597.text: I... I don't know what to say, V. But you're not facing this alone. We'll find a way, or we'll make sure the time you have left actually means something.

f-v3-river-ward-598.player: Check the roof, I will take the stairs.
f-v3-river-ward-598.text: Copy that. I'll clear the roof. Be careful on those stairs, V. I'll see you at the top.

f-v3-river-ward-599.player: I heard you ran away when things got hard.
f-v3-river-ward-599.text: That's a lie. I've stayed in the dirt longer than most people can handle. I'm curious, who's the one trying to rewrite my history for you?

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-600.player: You are useless in a fight, you know that?
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-600.text: I ran solo in this city long before you were a glimmer in a corporate lab. If you think my value is measured in how many bodies I drop in a street fight, you have no idea how this city actually works. Who told you I stopped knowing how to pull a trigger?

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-601.player: Rain again. Does this city ever dry out?
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-601.text: Not really. It just washes the grime from one street to the next. Makes the city feel smaller, if you let it.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-602.player: I just found out an old friend of mine died last night.
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-602.text: I am sorry, V. In this city, that is a conversation you eventually have too many times.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-603.player: Admit it, you were scared back there.
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-603.text: I don't do scared. I do calculations, and the math said we were in a bad spot. You always did mistake caution for shaking in the boots

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-604.player: We have ten minutes before the guards rotate. What is the plan?
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-604.text: Two exits, one vehicle, and someone watching the driver. You handle the breach, I'll coordinate the extraction. Now get moving.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-605.text: Careful, V. Flattery is a cheap currency, and I've always preferred something with a bit more value.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-606.player: Guess who just walked into the bar.
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-606.text: I can't see who you're talking about. Describe them, or tell me why it matters.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-607.player: Why should I trust a word you say?
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-607.text: Because in Night City, trust is a luxury you can't afford. You don't trust my word, you trust my track record. I keep my clients alive and my debts paid. That's the only guarantee that matters.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-608.player: What are you having for breakfast?
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-608.text: Black coffee and a cigarette. It is the only way to start the day without feeling the city crawling under my skin. You look like you haven't slept in two days.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-609.player: They shot him right in front of me and I could not do a thing.
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-609.text: That is a weight that doesn't go away, V. The only thing you can do now is make sure it doesn't happen again.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-610.player: Nice haircut. Did you lose a fight with a drone?
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-610.text: Still trying for the punchline, I see. Keep it up and you might actually find a way to make me laugh.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-611.player: I need you to cover the east entrance while I hack the terminal.
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-611.text: Done. Just make sure you are fast. If those guards catch us because you're fumbling with a keypad, we are going to have a very different conversation.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-612.player: I won the lottery. Three million eddies!
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-612.text: Three million. That is a lot of attention you do not want, and a very fast way to get a target on your back. Who knows you have it?

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-613.player: I cannot stop thinking about last night.
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-613.text: Then stop. Dwelling on it won't change the outcome, and it won't make you any faster on the draw.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-614.player: Everyone says you sold out. Did you?
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-614.text: Everyone says a lot of things in this city. I survived. If that looks like selling out to people who didn't make it past thirty, then so be it.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-615.player: What is your favorite place in Night City?
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-615.text: The Afterlife. It is the only place where the ghosts of the people I actually respected get to stay relevant.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-616.player: My place got torched. Everything I owned is gone.
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-616.text: That is a hard lesson in how fragile things are here. Possessions are just anchors, but I know it doesn't feel that way right now. Do you have a safe place to crash?

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-617.player: The shipment is two floors down. How do we get past security?
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-617.text: We don't go through the front. Find a service shaft or a ventilation duct. More guns won't fix a bad extraction, so give me a route that doesn't involve a firefight in a hallway.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-618.player: You snore like a busted turbine, did you know that?
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-618.text: Is that so? I'll be sure to remember that the next time you're complaining about the noise in the safehouse. Who exactly was listening close enough to notice?

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-619.player: The door was open and the whole place was empty.
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-619.text: That is not a coincidence. It is a invitation. Either they are waiting for you to walk in, or they already took what they wanted and left the door as a message.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-620.player: Stay a little longer. I like having you close.
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-620.text: You're getting bold, V. I'll stay for one more drink, but don't mistake a moment of quiet for a change in the rules.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-621.text: Enough to function. You're asking a lot of personal questions today. What is really on your mind?

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-622.player: Go on, say it to my face.
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-622.text: I don't need to shout to make a point. You're acting like a rookie looking for a fight, and frankly, it's boring.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-623.player: They know we are here. Orders?
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-623.text: Fall back to the secondary exit. Don't try to be a hero, just get to the vehicle. I'll cover the rear.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-624.player: I think I am losing my memory of my parents' faces.
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-624.text: That is a particular kind of hollow. The city has a way of erasing everything that doesn't serve a purpose. Just hold on to whatever fragments you have left.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-625.player: That thing I bought is alive. It is moving.
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-625.text: Moving how? If you bought something that breathes or thinks without a warranty, you didn't buy a tool, you bought a liability. Describe it.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-626.player: I bet you cannot go a whole day without complaining.
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-626.text: Is that a challenge? I can be as silent as a grave if the price is right. What are you betting?

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-627.player: I found a stray cat outside. Can I keep it?
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-627.text: A pet in this city is just another thing that can get hurt or get you killed. But if you can keep it fed and out of the way, I won't be the one to tell you no.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-628.player: Is it weird that I feel safe whenever you are around?
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-628.text: It is a dangerous feeling, V. Safety is an illusion in Night City, but if my presence helps you keep your head straight, then it serves a purpose.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-629.player: We got the data shard. Now what?
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-629.text: Get out of there and meet me at the rendezvous. Did you notice if anyone followed you, or was the exit as clean as you planned?

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-630.player: You are just like every other corpo lapdog.
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-630.text: Watch your mouth. I run the Afterlife, not a corporate boardroom. There is a difference between knowing how to play the game and being a dog on a leash.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-631.text: Some things are beyond our reach, V. The guilt is a heavy load, but carrying it won't bring her back. Just make sure you don't let it blind you to the people who are still here.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-632.player: Your old crew just called. They want you back.
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-632.text: The past has a habit of calling when it runs out of options. Who exactly was on the line?

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-633.player: Which is better, going in loud or quiet?
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-633.text: Quiet gets you the prize. Loud gets you a headline. Unless you have enough firepower to level the building, I suggest you find a way to be invisible.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-634.player: What would you do if I kissed you right now?
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-634.text: I would probably tell you that you have a very poor sense of timing. But I might just let you finish before I decide if I'm annoyed or amused.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-635.player: Careful, your soft side is showing.
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-635.text: Don't get used to it. A little bit of humanity doesn't mean I've forgotten how to be the one making the calls.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-636.player: Long day. Anything on your mind?
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-636.text: The usual. Too many mercs thinking they are legends and not enough of them knowing how to follow a simple plan. But for now, I am just thinking it is time for a drink.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-637.player: The doc says I do not have long.
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-637.text: That is the one contract none of us can negotiate. The question is how you spend the time you have left, and who you spend it with. Do you have a plan for the end?

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-638.player: Check the roof, I will take the stairs.
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-638.text: Understood. I will clear the top. If you get pinned on those stairs, don't expect me to come down and bail you out. Move.

f-v3-rogue-amendiares-639.player: I heard you ran away when things got hard.
f-v3-rogue-amendiares-639.text: I survived while the people who stayed to be martyrs became footnotes. There is a difference between running and knowing when a fight is already lost and choosing to live. Who is feeding you these stories?

f-v5-evelyn-parker-640.player: You are useless in a fight, you know that?
f-v5-evelyn-parker-640.text: I am aware. I prefer to let people like you handle the noise while I focus on the things that actually matter. I wonder if you enjoy the feeling of being the most dangerous person in the room.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-641.player: Rain again. Does this city ever dry out?
f-v5-evelyn-parker-641.text: Not really. It just changes from a drizzle to a flood, usually right when you have somewhere to be.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-642.player: I just found out an old friend of mine died last night.
f-v5-evelyn-parker-642.text: I am sorry to hear that, V. Night City has a way of making those losses feel sudden, even when you know the risks.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-643.player: Admit it, you were scared back there.
f-v5-evelyn-parker-643.text: I was cautious. There is a difference between being scared and knowing exactly how quickly things can go wrong.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-644.player: We have ten minutes before the guards rotate. What is the plan?
f-v5-evelyn-parker-644.text: We move in the gap between the shifts. If you can keep them distracted for just a few seconds, I can get the access we need without making a scene.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-645.text: Is that a compliment, or are you working your way toward a favor?

f-v5-evelyn-parker-646.player: Guess who just walked into the bar.
f-v5-evelyn-parker-646.text: I can't see right now, V. Who is it?

f-v5-evelyn-parker-647.player: Why should I trust a word you say?
f-v5-evelyn-parker-647.text: You shouldn't. Trust is a luxury in this city, and I would be suspicious of anyone asking for it for free.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-648.player: What are you having for breakfast?
f-v5-evelyn-parker-648.text: Something that doesn't come out of a vending machine, if I can find it. I have a particular weakness for real fruit, though it usually costs more than it is worth.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-649.player: They shot him right in front of me and I could not do a thing.
f-v5-evelyn-parker-649.text: That is a heavy thing to carry. The city likes to remind us, and often quite brutally, that some things are simply beyond our control.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-650.player: Nice haircut. Did you lose a fight with a drone?
f-v5-evelyn-parker-650.text: I prefer to think of it as a choice. Though I suspect you have a few stories of your own involving drones that didn't end quite so stylishly.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-651.player: I need you to cover the east entrance while I hack the terminal.
f-v5-evelyn-parker-651.text: I can do that. Just make sure you are fast, because I am not exactly built for a prolonged firefight.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-652.player: I won the lottery. Three million eddies!
f-v5-evelyn-parker-652.text: Three million. That is a dangerous amount of money to have in your pocket, and an even more dangerous amount to tell people about.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-653.player: I cannot stop thinking about last night.
f-v5-evelyn-parker-653.text: Some things are harder to shake than others. I suspect it is the part you cannot change that is keeping you awake.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-654.player: Everyone says you sold out. Did you?
f-v5-evelyn-parker-654.text: People love to label things they do not understand. I prefer to call it negotiating, and I have always been very good at the bargain.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-655.player: What is your favorite place in Night City?
f-v5-evelyn-parker-655.text: Anywhere quiet enough to hear myself think. Though a place with a decent menu and no one expecting anything from me is a rare luxury.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-656.player: My place got torched. Everything I owned is gone.
f-v5-evelyn-parker-656.text: That is a brutal way to start over. The only thing the city cannot take from you is the knowledge of who did it, and how you intend to answer.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-657.player: The shipment is two floors down. How do we get past security?
f-v5-evelyn-parker-657.text: We don't go through them. If we can find a service lift or a ventilation shaft, we can bypass the main checkpoints entirely.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-658.player: You snore like a busted turbine, did you know that?
f-v5-evelyn-parker-658.text: I have no idea what you are talking about. But if I do, I imagine it is just my way of reminding you that I am still here.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-659.player: The door was open and the whole place was empty.
f-v5-evelyn-parker-659.text: That is never a good sign. It usually means the real trap is the one you cannot see.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-660.player: Stay a little longer. I like having you close.
f-v5-evelyn-parker-660.text: That is a very dangerous thing to admit. I wonder if you are actually being sincere, or if you just enjoy the company of someone who knows how to keep a secret.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-661.text: Well enough. Though I suspect you spent half the night wondering if I was actually asleep or just listening to you toss and turn.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-662.player: Go on, say it to my face.
f-v5-evelyn-parker-662.text: I would, but I find that some things are far more effective when left unsaid. It keeps you guessing, and that is where the real leverage is.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-663.player: They know we are here. Orders?
f-v5-evelyn-parker-663.text: Then we stop pretending. Find the quickest exit and get us out of here before they close the perimeter.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-664.player: I think I am losing my memory of my parents' faces.
f-v5-evelyn-parker-664.text: That is a quiet kind of grief. The city has a way of erasing everything that does not serve a purpose, until you are left wondering what actually belonged to you.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-665.player: That thing I bought is alive. It is moving.
f-v5-evelyn-parker-665.text: I can't see what you are talking about, V. Describe it to me, or turn your vision on, because that sounds like a problem I would rather not be standing next to.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-666.player: I bet you cannot go a whole day without complaining.
f-v5-evelyn-parker-666.text: Is that a challenge? I could do it, but I suspect you would find the silence far more unsettling than my complaints.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-667.player: I found a stray cat outside. Can I keep it?
f-v5-evelyn-parker-667.text: A pet in this city. It is a sweet impulse, but I wonder if you have considered how a cat would react to the kind of life you lead.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-668.player: Is it weird that I feel safe whenever you are around?
f-v5-evelyn-parker-668.text: That is a very generous sentiment. Just be careful not to mistake my presence for a guarantee of safety, V. This city does not offer those.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-669.player: We got the data shard. Now what?
f-v5-evelyn-parker-669.text: Now we get it to someone who can actually read it. I wonder if the payout is still the same now that we know exactly what is on that shard.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-670.player: You are just like every other corpo lapdog.
f-v5-evelyn-parker-670.text: I have never been anyone's lapdog. I simply know how to speak their language so I can take what I need from them.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-671.text: Some burdens are too heavy to carry alone. The city makes us believe we can control everything, but sometimes the only thing left to do is figure out how to live with the silence.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-672.player: Your old crew just called. They want you back.
f-v5-evelyn-parker-672.text: They have a very short memory. I left for a reason, and I doubt they are offering anything that would make returning a sensible choice.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-673.player: Which is better, going in loud or quiet?
f-v5-evelyn-parker-673.text: Quiet is always better. Going in loud is just a way of telling everyone exactly where to find you, and I prefer to be the one doing the finding.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-674.player: What would you do if I kissed you right now?
f-v5-evelyn-parker-674.text: I would probably wonder if you were trying to distract me from something. But I suspect you would find that I am not as easy to rattle as you think.

f-v5-evelyn-parker-675.player: Careful, your soft side is showing.
